# Intake brief: Port the Vite watcher-ignore (`server.watch.ignored`) guard to sibling game repos' `vite.config.ts`

## Problem statement

The core scaffold template (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA) emits `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` (covering `**/.worklog/**` and the dev-output trees), and `tce-main-street` and `tce-the-rising` already carry the block — but 8 sibling game repos' checked-in `vite.config.ts` still lack it: `AI_Hell`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go`. When any of these repos accumulates `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (AI_Hell already has 9 + a nested `ToneForge` checkout), the Vite/Vitest file watcher recursively walks them and exhausts the host `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` budget — `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached` — crashing the dev server and breaking test runs (the exact failure mode fixed in the parent item MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY).

## Users

- **Developers/agents working in any Tableau-Card-Engine game repo** (tce-\*) — must be able to run `npm run dev` and `npm test` from the main checkout once worktrees exist without tripping the host watcher limit.
  - *User story:* "As a developer in tce-blackjack, I want my dev server to ignore `.worklog/worktrees/**` so a recursive watch never exhausts inotify (ENOSPC)."
- **AI_Hell maintainers** (in scope — Q1 answered) — same failure mode is already active (9 worktree checkouts).
  - *User story:* "As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same watcher guard, so my `vite` dev server survives `.worklog/worktrees/**` growth."
- **Verification/audit tooling** — full-suite runs in sibling repos must not fail with ENOSPC.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Watcher guard present in every in-scope repo's checked-in config.** The 7 tce-\* repos each import `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin` and set `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` with the template's explanatory comment (wording as in CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA / `tce-the-rising`). AI_Hell (if in scope) sets `watch.ignored` from a locally defined constant covering `**/.worklog/**` (plus its dev-output trees). Verified per repo by grep of the checked-in file — no in-scope repo may lack the block.
2. **Per-repo regression guard test (mirrors the core/main-street ENOSPC guard).** Each tce-\* repo gains `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (copy of main-street's, minus the in-process dev-server smoke; static assertions only): the real config imports the shared list, spreads it into `server.watch.ignored`, and the list covers `**/.worklog/**` plus `**/data/**`, `**/tmp/**`, `**/results/**`, `**/dist/**`. AI_Hell gains `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` asserting its local list covers `.worklog`. Each test is picked up by that repo's existing test projects and passes.
3. **Surgical port only.** No other template drift is synced: no `resolvePagesBase`/`base` backfill, no blind re-scaffold (sibling configs predate those template additions), no local-config changes (e.g. AI_Hell's `configCsvPlugin`, `open: true`, port settings) altered. Per-repo `git diff` touches only `vite.config.ts` plus the new guard test; pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes (`.gitignore`, untracked `AGENTS.md`/`.githooks/`/`.worklog/plugins/`) are never swept into a commit.
4. **Suites pass and changes land on each repo's `dev`.** Each in-scope repo's own test suite passes (agent-initiated runs go through the test skill, per repo), and each repo's change is committed on its `dev` branch and pushed to origin, with commits referencing `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` (precedent: cross-repo item MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV). The pre-existing 1-ahead-unpushed local commit on each sibling `dev` is accounted for at push time (see Constraints). tce-main-street itself has no source changes, so its suite is unaffected; full project suite (each modified repo) must pass with the changes.
5. **Documentation reflects the guard.** Config comment matches the core template wording; where a repo documents `npm run dev` (README/dev docs — currently none of the in-scope repos has a README), a matching note about the `.worklog/**` exclusion. CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **No core/TCE repository edits and no submodule moves.** The core scaffold template and its guard tests are already correct (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA completed) and every sibling's pinned core commit (`09723c4b`) already exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` in `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` — verified.
- **Surgical only** — do **not** blind re-scaffold (`npm run scaffold` / `scaffold:games`): the current template additionally emits `resolvePagesBase`/production `base` behaviour that the sibling configs do not have; a re-scaffold would change more than the watch block. Port the `server.watch.ignored` block + import only.
- **Cross-repo working-tree isolation.** This item lives in tce-main-street's worklog but touches 8 sibling checkouts, all outside the tce-main-street worktree. Precedent MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV ("Cross-repo change ... Pushed to sibling dev") governs: edit each sibling checkout directly, commit per repo on its own `dev`, push per repo. tce-main-street's own worktree/main checkout stays untouched (no tce-main-street source change → no implement-worktree changes expected).
- **Respect pre-existing dirt.** Each sibling has unrelated uncommitted changes (`.gitignore` edits; untracked `AGENTS.md`, `.githooks/`, `.worklog/plugins/`). Never commit them; stage only `vite.config.ts` (+ new test).
- **Sibling `dev` is 1 commit ahead of origin** (an unpushed `.worklog/config.yaml` CTA commit, `WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS`). Pushing the port will carry that commit; if a non-fast-forward/push rejection occurs, resolve against that known baseline (do not rewrite others' pushed history).
- **Test-execution policy:** all agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill — run per repo (each sibling has its own CWD/worklog), never ad-hoc `npm test`/`vitest`.

## Existing state

- **Scaffolded siblings (7):** `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go` — `vite.config.ts` is AUTO-GENERATED (scaffold `renderViteConfig`), identical to each other apart from the game name in the header comment, and each `server:` block has `port: 3000, open: false` only — no `watch.ignored`. Verified: `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` absent from all 7.
- **AI_Hell (1):** bespoke hand-written config (port 5173, `open: true`, `configCsvPlugin`, no `core` submodule) — no `server.watch` at all; it **cannot** import the core list. It already has 9 `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (+ nested `ToneForge` checkout) — the ENOSPC failure mode is live there.
- **Exemplars:** `tce-main-street/vite.config.ts` and `tce-the-rising/vite.config.ts` already carry the block (main-street also has `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`, the regression pattern to mirror; core has `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` static guard).
- Siblings' core submodules are clean and pinned at `v0.1.17-201-g09723c4b`, which exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`. Their `npm test` = `vitest run --project unit` with `include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`, and tsconfig includes `tests/**/*.ts` — new config tests are picked up automatically.

## Desired change

- **Per tce-\* repo:** in `vite.config.ts`, add `import { DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS } from './core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin';` and extend the `server:` block with `watch: { ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS] }` + the template's ENOSPC comment; add `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (static assertions copied from main-street's guard).
- **AI_Hell (in scope — Q1 answered):** add a locally defined ignore constant (e.g. `vite/watchIgnore.ts`) mirroring the core list (or a scoped `.worklog`-focused list), wire `server: { watch: { ignored: [...] } }` into `vite.config.ts`, and add `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts`.
- Single source of truth stays in core; nothing in `core/` changes.

## Key Files:

- Each tce-\* repo: `vite.config.ts` — add `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` import + `server.watch.ignored` block
- Each tce-\* repo: `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (new) — static config-wiring + pattern-coverage guard (mirror of `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` ENOSPC assertions and main-street's `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`)
- AI_Hell: `vite.config.ts` — wire `watch.ignored`; `vite/watchIgnore.ts` (new) — local ignore constant; `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (new) — guard test (AI_Hell test roots: `src`, `scripts`, `vite`)
- Reference only (no change): `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (template already correct), `core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` (`DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` source), `tce-main-street/tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (guard pattern to mirror)

## Related work

- MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY — Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (**parent; completed**; this item is its derived sibling port)
- CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA — core: `game-repo-scaffold` renderViteConfig omits `server.watch.ignored` (completed; template now emits it)
- CG-0MTJ7A4Z3000MFMV / CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC — core: vite-transcript-plugin ENOSPC hardening (completed)
- MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C — [test-failure] suite-exit failure (completed; same root cause family)
- MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG — Main Street vite-node CLI test flake (completed; the local isolation that a blind re-scaffold would regress)
- MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV — Cross-repo change precedent: tracked in main-street worklog, "Pushed to sibling dev" AC (completed)
- MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV / MS-0MUQZH53F004ZKAN — Core scaffold Pages-base work (completed; the template drift deliberately **not** backfilled here)
- Note: sibling repos have their own worklog stores (some without a DB on disk); no sibling-side work items exist for this change — the main-street item is the tracking point.

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption (Q1 answered: include AI_Hell):** AI_Hell is in scope, handled via a locally defined ignore constant because it has no `core` submodule from which to import the shared list.
- **Risk (low):** chokidar ignore-glob semantics — `**/.worklog/**` covers `.worklog/worktrees/**`; validated by the core regression suite and main-street's in-process smoke. Sibling guards use the same static assertions.
- **Risk (medium):** list duplication in AI_Hell drifts from core over time — mitigation: comment in `vite/watchIgnore.ts` pointing at the core source (single source of truth), and the guard test pins `.worklog` coverage.
- **Risk (medium):** per-repo dev-server smoke tests ×8 would be slow/flaky under suite contention — mitigation: ship **static** config-wiring guards per repo (mirroring `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`); the in-process `server.watcher.getWatched()` smoke stays where it already exists (main-street) — no new dev-server startups in siblings.
- **Risk (low):** push non-fast-forward on 7 sibling `dev` branches (each 1 local commit ahead of origin) — known baseline commit; rebase/stacking acceptable since those commits are local-only; surface anything unexpected rather than force-pushing.
- **Scope-creep risk:** syncing other stale template drift (`resolvePagesBase`/production `base`, `unit-cli` isolations, etc.) to siblings, or host inotify tuning, is tempting — recorded as related work (MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV etc.), NOT this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: **Is AI_Hell in scope?** Its `vite.config.ts` is hand-written (not scaffold-generated), it has no `core` submodule, so the shared `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` list cannot be imported — the port there requires a locally duplicated ignore constant (drift risk), though its failure mode is already live (9 worktrees).
  - Options: (a) **Include AI_Hell** with a local ignore constant + guard test — rec, because the producer explicitly listed it and its ENOSPC risk is already active; (b) Exclude AI_Hell — port only the 7 scaffolded tce-\* repos and file a derived item in AI_Hell's own worklog (AH- prefix); (c) Include AI_Hell only if it adopts the core submodule (large, out of scope).
  - **Recommended:** (a) Include AI_Hell with a locally defined constant (comment referencing core as canonical source), pending producer confirmation.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-21):** Option **(a) — include AI_Hell** with a locally defined ignore constant + guard test, plus (as an additional ask) a follow-up work item in AI_Hell to bring its testing framework in line with the other repos. **Status: answered/closed.**
- Priority/type: kept `bug` / `low` as set — same root-cause family as parent MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY (reclassified chore→bug); `low` retained because for the 7 tce-\* repos with zero current worktrees the failure is latent, not actively blocking (AI_Hell's live state argues medium should AI_Hell be confirmed in scope).
- Research summary: verified all 8 repos lack the block (grep of checked-in configs); the 7 tce-\* configs are otherwise identical scaffold output (only the game name differs); each sibling's pinned core commit (`09723c4b`) already exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`; `tce-the-rising` is the wired exemplar; main-street's `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` is the guard pattern to mirror; AI_Hell's test roots are `src`/`scripts`/`vite` with an exhaustive project-membership classifier (vite/ test auto-classified as unit). Cross-repo commit/push precedent: MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** – Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (completed)
- **MS-0MUQZH45Y001OGBK** – Pages base-path build tests (completed)
- **MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV** – Core scaffold template Pages base (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: beleaguered, blackjack, blind, block, castle (+38 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: beleaguered, blackjack, block, castle, checked (+32 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mv5sehhg000zkua, beleaguered, blackjack, block, castle (+27 more)


## Plan

**Decomposition (8 parallel children — one per in-scope repo).** Each child is a
vertical slice through all layers for its repo: config wiring + regression guard
test + suite run through the test skill + commit/push on `dev` + commit recorded.
All children are independent (no dependency edges) — each repo's port is
self-contained, so the 7 scaffolded tce-\* ports can proceed in any order and
AI_Hell proceeds in parallel. Test-first ordering applies within each child
(guard test written before/with the config wiring).

| # | Child | Repo | Priority | Scope |
|---|-------|------|----------|-------|
| 1 | Port Vite watcher-ignore guard to tce-beleaguered-castle vite.config.ts (MS-0MVSXXRZE00691IY) | tce-beleaguered-castle | low | import shared list + `server.watch.ignored` + static guard test |
| 2 | Port Vite watcher-ignore guard to tce-blackjack vite.config.ts (MS-0MVSXXSMV003XKGI) | tce-blackjack | low | same |
| 3 | Port Vite watcher-ignore guard to tce-coloretto vite.config.ts (MS-0MVSXXTCJ001V1AB) | tce-coloretto | low | same |
| 4 | Port Vite watcher-ignore guard to tce-feudalism vite.config.ts (MS-0MVSXXU46009YCAJ) | tce-feudalism | low | same |
| 5 | Port Vite watcher-ignore guard to tce-golf vite.config.ts (MS-0MVSXXUTW000P8FR) | tce-golf | low | same |
| 6 | Port Vite watcher-ignore guard to tce-lost-cities vite.config.ts (MS-0MVSXXVKP005CHSM) | tce-lost-cities | low | same |
| 7 | Port Vite watcher-ignore guard to tce-sushi-go vite.config.ts (MS-0MVSXXW9R007XPG8) | tce-sushi-go | low | same |
| 8 | Port Vite watcher-ignore guard to AI_Hell vite.config.ts (local constant) (MS-0MVT0MBI7008B0N9) | AI_Hell | medium | local `vite/watchIgnore.ts` + wire `watch.ignored` + `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` |

**Design decisions.**
- The 7 scaffolded tce-\* repos import the shared `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`
  from their pinned core submodule (single source of truth; no list
  duplication). AI_Hell has no core submodule, so it duplicates the list
  locally in `vite/watchIgnore.ts` with a comment naming the core source as
  canonical (producer-confirmed option (a), Q1).
- Guards are **static** per repo (mirroring `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`) — no
  per-repo dev-server smoke tests (8 startups would be slow/flaky under suite
  contention); the in-process `server.watcher.getWatched()` smoke stays where it
  already exists in tce-main-street.
- **Surgical only:** no `resolvePagesBase`/`base` backfill, no blind
  re-scaffold, no changes to AI_Hell's `configCsvPlugin`/`telemetryUploadPlugin`
  /`open`/port.
- **Cross-repo isolation (precedent MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV):** each sibling
  checkout is edited/committed/pushed directly on its own `dev`; the
  tce-main-street worktree is untouched (no tce-main-street source change).
  Pre-existing dirt (`.gitignore`, untracked `AGENTS.md`/`.githooks/`/
  `.worklog/plugins/`, AI_Hell's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`) is never
  staged.
- Each sibling `dev` is 1 commit ahead of origin (`WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS`); the

**Test-first ordering.** Within each child the regression guard test is written
before/with the config wiring; there is no separate test-feature child because
the test is a one-file static guard that ships in the same slice as the config.

**Vertical slice phasing.** Each child delivers end-to-end for its repo (config,
test, suite, commit, push), so there is no horizontal phasing — the 8 children
are 8 independent vertical slices.

## Plan: changelog

  (7 scaffolded tce-\* + AI_Hell), no dependency edges; AC5 (documentation)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan)

- No new clarifying questions were required. The intake Appendix already

# Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

## Headline

The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait in
`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` is already at the largest
budget the 60 s browser hook permits (40 000 ms = 16 000 ms cap + 24 000 ms
margin + 20 000 ms boot = 60 000 ms), yet it fails at ≈2× CPU oversubscription
because the bounded end-of-turn deferral is re-polled on Phaser's clamped game
clock, so the forced day start is detected late. **Decision: make the
deferral's safety cap starvation-proof** — one extracted helper whose deadline
and re-poll run on wall clock, enforced even while the page is not painting
(producer, Q1 = C, Q2 = 1).

## Problem statement

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate passes 20/20 quiet
(peak load 15.3), passes 2/2 at 8 burners (peak 23.6), and fails exactly one
wait — `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` — at load ≥ ≈31
(≈2× oversubscription, 16 burners, peak 32.8). That wait's budget is already at
the ceiling the 60 s hook permits, so no poll-budget tweak inside the hook can
rescue it.

Root cause (mechanism, verified against the installed `phaser` source):
Phaser's `TimeStep` clamps the per-frame delta it feeds scenes — under
`smoothStep` (default on) each frame contributes at most `1000/fps.min`
(200 ms) — and `Clock.elapsed`, which drives `delayedCall` timers and tween
progress, advances by that clamped delta. Under starvation (a few frames per
second) all game-time-paced choreography stretches: income phase gaps, coin
flights, the incident hold, and the deferral's own 250 ms `delayedCall`
re-polls. The deferral *deadline* (`s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`,
where `s.time.now` is the raw frame timestamp) is wall-clock, but it is only
re-checked at those clamped polls, so the forced day start is delayed by the
same starvation. Aggregate: closing choreography (stretched) + 16 s cap
(late-detected) + boot > the 40 s budget and the 60 s hook.

The cap's stated purpose is "end-of-turn can never hang the game"
(CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q, AC5/AC7). A stall bound that is only observed at frame
boundaries does not provide that guarantee — which is what this item fixes,
without touching the user-visible pacing.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer / gate runner** on the shared dev host: needs the browser
  gate green; a red `MainStreetScene` suite at ≈2× oversubscription burns whole
  sessions on retries and blocks the build → test → commit order.
- **Maintainer triaging a red browser suite**: needs a red wait to mean a
  behavioural regression, not host weather.
- **Release engineer** on the dev-push gate: a red gate on a loaded shared host
  stalls shipping even when the scene is correct.
- **Players**: unchanged pacing — the choreography, the incident hold and the
  cap value all stay as shipped; only the cap's *enforcement* becomes
  wall-clock rather than frame-clock, so under starvation the day advances at
  the documented bound instead of stalling past it.

Example user stories:

> As an agent running the browser gate on the shared 16-core host, I want the
> Enter-to-end-turn wait to pass at any load the host actually reaches, so that
> my gate result does not depend on which sibling suites happen to be running.

> As a player whose machine is momentarily overloaded, I want the end-of-turn
> to still advance within the documented safety window, so that the game can
> never appear hung.

## Existing state

- Measured envelope (2026-10-24, 16-core shared host): quiet 20/20 pass
  (peak 15.3); 8 burners 2/2 pass, then one fail at ambient 31.3; 16 burners
  fail at the 40 000 ms end-of-turn budget. Every other wait in the file passes
  at that load.
- The wait's effective budget is `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (16 000) +
  `floorMs: END_TURN_STARVATION_MARGIN_MS` (24 000) = 40 000 ms, the largest
  that keeps the documented 20 000 ms scene-boot allowance inside the 60 s
  `testTimeout` (asserted by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`). The
  suite's per-test timeout is already `it(..., 60_000)`.
- Five deferral polls race the choreography, all with the same shape
  (`startAt = <scene clock> + cap`, then `delayedCall(250, poll)`):
  3 in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`advanceTurn` ~433,
  forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) and 2 in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` (`finish`'s income wait
  ~254 and the reveal gating ~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` already has the
  degradation precedent: `scheduleOrRun` runs the callback immediately when the
  scene has no clock (headless), which a wall-clock helper must preserve.
- Node unit suites drive these polls through fake `time` stubs
  (`tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`), and
  `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` pins "exactly three
  `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" by regex — both must be
  updated by the extraction.
- Reduced motion clears `incomeCollectionActive` synchronously in
  `MainStreetAnimatorIncome` (~line 1039), but it is **not** the remedy chosen:
  the parent rejected it as the sole remedy because it removes the
  deferred-income path from coverage.

## Desired change (decision: option C)

Replace the five duplicated deferral polls with **one shared, injectable
helper** that:

1. computes its deadline from a wall-clock timestamp (`Date.now()`),
2. re-polls with a wall-clock timer (`window.setTimeout`), not the scene clock,
3. forces completion (clearing `incomeCollectionActive` and invoking the
   caller's continuation) once `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time has
   elapsed since the deferral began,
4. is enforced even when the page is not painting — a backgrounded/hidden
   document ahead of the cap forces the advance rather than waiting for the
   next animation frame (Q2 = 1), and
5. degrades to today's behaviour where no clock/timer exists (headless node
   scenes run the continuation immediately), and exposes its clock/timer for
   deterministic unit driving.

Options considered and rejected (recorded for traceability):

- **A — accept and document the envelope** (no code change): the gate can still
  go red on the shared host when ambient load spikes ≥2×, conflicting with the
  "red tree never pushed" policy; rejected in favour of a root-cause fix.
- **B — reduced-motion Enter test + a separate cheap deferral-contract test**:
  no production change, but downgrades the file's end-to-end end-of-turn test
  to a synthetic and couples coverage to a reduced-motion implementation
  detail; retained only as a fallback if C's soak does not pass.
- **D — raise the browser hook for this test**: pure masking, requires
  amending the parent's "any derived budget must leave headroom for boot plus
  teardown within that hook" AC and re-baselining the guard's headroom rule,
  and would fail again at ≈4× oversubscription; rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **One bounded-deferral helper, wall-clock enforced.** All five
      income-collection deferral polls route through a single shared helper
      whose deadline is wall clock and whose re-poll is a wall timer; no inline
      `s.time.delayedCall(250, <poll>)` / `<scene clock> + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
      poll remains. A unit test with a frozen scene clock and an advancing wall
      clock proves the continuation is forced within one poll interval of the
      16 000 ms cap.
- [ ] **Forced advance is not tied to paint.** When the document is hidden / no
      frame runs, the cap still forces the advance after the cap elapses
      (Q2 = 1). A unit test asserts the wall timer — not the scene clock —
      drives the assertion, and the behaviour is documented in the module's
      code comment.
- [ ] **Injectable and backward-compatible.** The helper accepts an injectable
      clock/timer (so `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
      `turnflow.test.ts` and the new tests drive it deterministically) and
      preserves today's no-clock degradation (headless scenes run the
      continuation immediately).
- [ ] **Single source of truth for the cap.** `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays
      16 000 and remains the only cap value; the
      `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` "exactly three
      `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" pin is updated to the
      helper extraction (asserting the helper consumes the constant), so the
      duplication cannot silently return.
- [ ] **No production pacing change.** The choreography timing constants
      (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`, flight/stagger durations, `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`)
      and the cap value are unchanged — pinned by existing/added unit tests;
      only the cap's enforcement mechanism differs.
- [ ] **Wait-budget guard still green.** `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`
      passes unchanged: the end-of-turn wait keeps its cap-derived 40 000 ms
      budget and `budget + 20 s boot ≤ 60 s` headroom rule. If the soak shows
      the budget can now be reduced, that reduction is a *derived* margin
      change proved by the soak, not a hand-picked literal.
- [ ] **Reliability proven, not assumed.** `/skill:test --type soak-load`
      (≥ `nproc` burners) passes with the change, and the pre-change failure at
      the same burner count is reproduced and recorded on this item; both
      before/after tables (burners, peak load, runs, wall times, summary paths)
      are posted as a comment.
- [ ] **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope" and
      the headroom rule section record the decision (cap enforced on wall
      clock, hidden-tab semantics) and the post-fix envelope, replacing the
      "above ~2× is outside the envelope" caveat with measured evidence; the
      helper's module comment documents the wall-clock contract. All related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
      README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes
      (`/skill:test --type full`), evidence recorded on this item.

## Constraints

- **No behavioural change to production pacing.** The choreography, the
  incident hold and the cap value are shipped features
  (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q); only the cap's enforcement may
  change.
- The parent's headroom constraint stands: `budget + scene-boot allowance` must
  stay inside the browser 60 s hook.
- Reduced motion must not become the sole remedy (parent decision); the
  deferred-income path keeps explicit coverage.
- All five deferral sites must keep identical semantics after extraction, and
  the existing fake-clock unit suites must not be weakened to accommodate the
  change.
- A stale wall timer must never fire into a destroyed scene — reuse the
  existing `scene.isActive()` / try-catch defensive pattern from the deferred
  closing tail.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill only
  (`/skill:test --type soak-load`, `--type full`); no ad-hoc `npx vitest` loops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — add the shared
  wall-clock deferral helper (sibling to `scheduleOrRun` ~line 176); adopt it in
  `finish`'s income wait (~254) and the reveal gating (~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — three deferral sites
  (`advanceTurn` ~433, forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) adopt the
  helper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
  unchanged; comment updated to state the wall-clock enforcement contract.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` — the "exactly three
  `s.time.now + cap` sites" regex pin moves to the helper extraction.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — fake `time` stubs: drive the injected
  timer/clock.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — Enter test and its
  40 000 ms margin expected unchanged.
- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` — headroom rule re-check (expected
  unchanged).
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — "Measured envelope" + headroom rule: record the
  decision and the post-fix soak evidence.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the clamped-delta mechanism is the dominant starvation link
  and the deferral's poll cadence is the part that can be fixed without touching
  pacing. Verified against the installed Phaser source
  (`TimeStep.smoothDelta`, `Clock.now` / `Clock.elapsed` semantics); the
  before/after `soak-load` run is the confirmation.
- **Risk:** removing the late-detection link may not be sufficient on its own —
  the choreography phases before/after the deferral still stretch under
  clamped delta. Mitigation: the soak is a hard AC; if it still fails, the
  fallback is option B's separate deferral-contract test (not option D), and
  the residual envelope is re-documented with evidence.
- **Risk (accepted, decided):** a wall-clock cap changes hidden/backgrounded-tab
  behaviour — the day start is now forced after the cap instead of stalling
  until the tab paints again (Q2 = 1). This is the intended semantics of a stall
  bound; documented in the module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.
- **Risk:** a wall timer outliving the scene could fire into a destroyed scene.
  Mitigation: `scene.isActive()` guard plus the existing try-catch pattern; a
  unit test covers the destroyed/stale case.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the attractor is "rework all game-time animation off
  clamped delta" (tweens, phase gaps, incident hold). Explicitly out of scope —
  record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG — this item (`discovered-from:` the soak child
  MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L; soak evidence and envelope recorded there and in
  `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope").
- MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — parent: made the file's waits load-tolerant via
  cap-derived budgets; its headroom AC and "Measured limit (triaged, not a
  flake)" section are the origin of this item.
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — the 20-run / under-load soak whose evidence defines the
  envelope and whose `soak-load` profile proves this fix.
- MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P — the wait-budget guard and headroom rule this item must
  keep green.
- MS-0MUYFX7Q2004JQ5R — shared end-of-turn closing presentation primitive that
  carries `incomeCollectionCapMs`.
- CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ / CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q — phased income choreography and
  deferred income window (untouched pacing; the property the cap protects).
- MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (open) — planned End-of-Turn summary dialog on the
  closing completion path; it will interact with the deferral this item
  extracts, so check dependency direction during planning.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L** – Prove browser-wait reliability: 20-run soak plus under-load run (completed)
- **MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P** – Guard browser wait budgets against production caps (completed)
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary… (open; planned dialog on the closing path)

### Related repository files
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine developer guide; frame-loop/delta context.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — measured envelope and headroom rule this item updates.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — documents reduced motion, deferral pacing and
  presentation behaviour these waits must respect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Given the measured envelope (the gate fails only above ≈2× CPU
  oversubscription, load ≥ ~31), which remediation should this item
  implement — (A) accept and document the envelope with no code change,
  (B) convert the Enter test to reduced motion plus a separate cheap
  deferral-contract test, (C) make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof (wall-clock deadline + wall-clock poll, one extracted
  helper, production change confined to the safety cap), or (D) raise the
  browser hook for this test (parent AC amendment needed)?"
  — Answer (producer): **C** — make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof. Source: interactive reply (intake interview round 1,
  2026-10-25). Agent recommendation was C (stated with rationale before the
  answer); A was recorded as the zero-production-change fallback and B's second
  variant as the fallback if C's soak still fails. Research behind the
  recommendation: Phaser `TimeStep.smoothDelta` clamps per-frame delta to
  `1000/fps.min` (200 ms default), so under rAF starvation the choreography and
  the deferral's 250 ms `delayedCall` re-polls both run at a fraction of
  wall-clock speed — the wall-clock cap deadline is therefore detected late,
  which is the link C removes.
- Q2 (conditional on C): "Should the 16 000 ms cap be enforced against wall
  clock even when the page is not painting/visible (backgrounded tab or fully
  starved rAF — the day start is forced after 16 s wall even though the
  choreography never ran), or should the forced advance hold while the document
  is hidden/blurred and resume on visibility change?"
  — Answer (producer): **as recommended** = enforce on wall clock (option 1):
  the cap is a stall bound, nothing is visible while hidden, and today a hidden
  tab already stalls the animator indefinitely. Source: interactive reply
  (intake interview round 1, 2026-10-25). Recorded as an accepted, documented
  semantic change in the Risks section and to be reflected in the helper's
  module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.

# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger; additions are optional and backwards-compatible — `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.
4. Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the engine/headless close path; checkpoint save ordering (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged, and the dialog adds no save and mutates no state.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests, and a competitive-mode browser dialog test); **all related documentation is updated** (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md competitive closing and end-of-turn summary sections, plus any README/dev references); **the full project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (outbound dependency): the parent item is
  still `open` (stage `intake_complete`) — its `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger
  does **not exist in the code yet**. This item builds on and consumes that
  ledger; implementers must land/coordinate with the parent first. Per-seat
  expense capture does not exist anywhere today — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  returns `void` and only logs — so the per-seat ledger extension is real
  engine work on top of the parent's ledger shape (kept optional and
  backwards-compatible throughout).
- Presentation-only contract: the dialog reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In competitive, deltas are
  already applied to each `PlayerRecord` before the closing is presented, so
  the panel shows post-round values; the checkpoint save stays in
  `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (existing ordering).
- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices) exactly as the parent
  item constrains: `createOverlayBackground` + `createOverlayButton` from
  `@ui`; elements parented into `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201;
  everything pushed into `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance
  (reduced-motion safe); button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- Headless determinism and bounded pacing must not regress: Monte-Carlo /
  AI headless days (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`)
  never invoke the scene presentation and must never show/block on the dialog;
  the competitive closing bound (`COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`) stays.
- **Assumption (Q-scope, from repo evidence):** a "round" equals **one
  completed shared day** — all non-eliminated seats finished and the shared
  closing ran. The engine has no separate "round" concept beyond the shared
  day (`round-robin` seat iteration only), so "one panel per completed round"
  = one dialog per shared day.
- **Assumption (blocking safety):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one device
  (no networked multiplayer), so a blocking dialog gated on the single human
  seat cannot stall other humans. Interactive Q1 = A.
- The parent item's banking-hint ordering assumption is single-player-only and
  does not apply to the competitive panel (no banking-hint step exists in the
  competitive closing).
- `TurnResult` / `OwnerIncomeResult` additions must not break competitive
  callers (`MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing`,
  `perSeatClosingSummary`, scoreboard/HUD consumers) — keep ledger fields
  optional/absent-undefined-safe and guard with tests.

## Existing state

- `endCompetitiveTurnDay` (`src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`):
  ends the human's MarketPhase, drives AI seats to the shared closing, runs
  `runCompetitiveClosing`, then `presentCompetitiveDayTail` →
  station checkpoint save → `presentCompetitiveClosing(closing, () =>
  startTurnPhase())`. The new gate slots at the end of the closing
  presentation, before `startTurnPhase` (presentation path only).
- `TurnResult.playerIncome?: OwnerIncomeResult[]` **already exists**
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`): owner-keyed income, non-eliminated seats,
  in seat order, populated by `applyCompetitiveIncome`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, through `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`
  in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`). Each entry carries
  `income.phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` (base / synergy / reputation /
  events / upcoming slots per owner).
- Per-seat ongoing costs are computed in `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) — staff salaries per owner, community +
  business running costs per slot owner via `ownerTaggedGrid` — but are
  **not surfaced** on any result (void, log-only). Businesses owned per seat
  are derivable from `ownerTaggedGrid` / `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`).
- Per-seat row conventions exist in `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`): `You` / `AI n` labels,
  `resolveSeatColour` seat colours, coin/rep/score columns — reused by the
  Game Over overlay model `MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`.
- Overlay precedent and single-player dialog model come from
  MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (its `MainStreetTurnSummary` model +
  `showTurnSummaryDialog`); docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md documents the
  competitive closing presentation (section "Competitive phase-major closing
  presentation …"), including the current auto-advance behaviour that this
  item changes.

## Desired change

1. Engine: capture and surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult` —
   per-owner ongoing expenses (staff / community / business), businesses
   owned, net coin change — extending the `OwnerIncomeResult` shape (or the
   parent's owner-keyed ledger) inside `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` /
   `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`; keep everything optional so
   single-player, N=1 and headless calls are untouched.
2. Model: extend the single-player Phaser-free `MainStreetTurnSummary` to
   render **owner-keyed competitive rows** (seat label + colour from the
   competitive scoreboard conventions) for the round just closed.
3. UI: extend the single-player `showTurnSummaryDialog(...)` (or a thin
   competitive sibling sharing the same panel) with **[ Next Turn ]**
   (primary) and a **disabled [ Bank Loan ]** button behind the shared wiring
   seam; gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` so the deferred
   (animations-enabled) path presents the dialog when the closing completes
   and only calls `startTurnPhase` after **[ Next Turn ]** — reduced-motion /
   replay / headless keep today's auto-advance.
4. Tests and docs: Phaser-free model tests, engine per-seat ledger tests, a
   competitive browser dialog test; update docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md
   (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections).

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` on the dialog (between closing-complete and `startTurnPhase`); presentation path only
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` / `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`: surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`: return/capture the per-owner expense breakdown (staff / community / business)
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnResult` (and/or `OwnerIncomeResult`) with the optional owner-keyed round ledger (expenses, businesses owned, net change)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` / `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `OwnerIncomeResult` shape extension
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend the Phaser-free summary model to render owner-keyed competitive rows (reusing scoreboard label/colour conventions)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` + `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — dialog presentation + delegation (shared with the single-player panel); `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` per overlay conventions
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — reuse `You` / `AI n` labels, `resolveSeatColour` colours for rows
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` (pure model), `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` (engine), `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` (competitive overlay)

## Related work

### Automated related-work report (`find_related.py`)

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary dialog (single-player seed)
  (open)
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** – Bank Loans (open)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove
  single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback
  (completed)
- Repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `core/AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (keyword overlap: competitive,
  ledger, end-of-turn, dialog, seat, round, businesses).
- Duplicate check: `wl search "turn summary competitive"` returned only the
  parent, the deferred Bank Loans seam and End of game stats — **no
  overlapping completed item**; no duplicate/partial-overlap rewrite needed.

### Hand-curated context

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — **parent / blocked-by**: single-player End of Turn
  summary dialog + `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger; this item's panel consumes
  that ledger and the parent's overlay/model. Not yet implemented (open,
  intake_complete) — ordering constraint.
- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — **Bank Loans**: the seam this item's disabled Bank
  Loan button exposes; enablement blocked by that item (shared with
  single-player panel).
- `MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` — **End of game stats** (open, low): turn-by-turn
  history + graphs on Game Over; consumes the same per-turn ledger data
  (synergy, not duplication — distinct screen).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` (completed) — end-of-turn presentation refactor:
  source of today's `closingSummary` / shared closing primitive.
- `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` + `MS-0MUYFXA36009EMH0` (completed) — competitive
  per-seat income choreography and per-seat animated closing: the cadence this
  panel extends; `TurnResult.playerIncome` originates here.
- `MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM` (completed) — game-over overlay epic: the
  Phaser-free-model + overlay-convention precedent (`MainStreetGameOverSummary`
  reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (round = day):** "one panel per completed round" maps to one
  panel per completed shared day (every seat finished + closing ran); the
  engine has no separate round concept. Recorded from repo evidence; if a
  day-vs-round distinction exists conceptually (e.g. a preset defining round
  length), the panel cadence would need revisiting — flagged for implementer
  verification.
- **Assumption (single human seat):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one
  device, so a blocking dialog on the human's **[ Next Turn ]** cannot stall
  other humans; multifloored safety holds for the current product shape.
  (If networked multiplayer ever lands, blocking semantics need a per-seat
  pause protocol.)
- **Risk (parent not landed):** the owner-keyed ledger this item consumes does
  not exist yet; if the parent lands without the per-seat expense capture
  (today `void`/log-only), this item must extend it — keep additions optional
  and guarded so `presentCompetitiveClosing` and headless/Monte-Carlo flows are
  byte-stable when absent.
- **Risk (blocking regresses headless pacing):** the gate must live in the
  scene presentation tail only (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`), never in engine
  close functions; Monte-Carlo / AI headless days never touch the scene and
  must continue to auto-advance under `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`.
- **Risk (eliminated seats):** the closing already omits eliminated seats from
  `playerIncome`; the panel must render exactly the seats the closing surfaced
  (no ghost rows for bankrupt/eliminated seats) and say so in its test.
- **Risk (loans are per-owner):** the shared disabled Bank Loan seam is a
  single hook today; when MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG lands, competitive loans are
  likely per-seat — keep the seam shaped so it can become
  `onBankLoanAction(seatId)` without re-plumbing the panel.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-round history across days (post-game stats,
  MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV), networked multiplayer, live loans
  (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG) and any round-summary log/graph features are outside
  this item; tracked as linked items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Blocking behaviour — in single-player the dialog blocks the next-day
  advance until [ Next Turn ] is clicked; in competitive the day currently
  auto-advances after the closing presentation. Options: A) Block like
  single-player — next day starts only after [ Next Turn ]. B) Non-blocking —
  panel appears but the day advances behind it / auto-dismisses."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — consistency
  with the single-player dialog; accepted as chosen.)
- Q2: "Per-seat data source — per-seat expenses aren't captured anywhere
  today (TurnResult.playerIncome covers income only). Options: A) Extend the
  engine with an owner-keyed per-seat ledger on TurnResult (per-seat ongoing
  costs, businesses owned, net change — engine-computed, testable headless),
  mirroring the parent's ledger. B) Derive presentation-only at panel time
  from committed state."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — matches the
  parent item's owner-keyed ledger design intent; accepted as chosen.)
- Q3: "Bank Loan button parity — the single-player dialog renders a disabled
  [ Bank Loan ] button with a wiring seam for MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG. Options:
  A) Same disabled Bank Loan button in the competitive panel (parity).
  B) Omit it — strictly the seed's content."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — one shared
  loans seam avoids divergent affordances; accepted as chosen.)

# Intake brief: Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** low · **Cross-repo:** yes (Tableau-Card-Engine core via the `./core` submodule) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL

## Problem statement

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declares two npm scripts — `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` — that point at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, a file that does **not** exist in a game repo (Option C: game repos have no root `scripts/` tree; the scaffold lives in the core at `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`). Invoking either script fails with a module-not-found error. The working game-repo entry point, `npm run scaffold`, passes `--core-root ./core` and exists in every generated repo.

Root cause (resolved): `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherits the **entire** core `scripts` map from the core manifest (line ~280: `...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(manifest.scripts ?? {}))`). `core/package.json` legitimately declares `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` for core-repo use, so both leak unmodified into every generated game repo. The description's open "which is true" question is answered: the template **does** emit them, but only by inheritance — the fix is a template-side filter, not merely deleting two lines from each repo.

## Users

- **Game-repo maintainers (agents and humans)** — run npm scripts inside a game repo without tripping over dead entries.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold:game` to either work or not be declared, so a script listed in my repo never fails with module-not-found."
- **Core scaffold owners (Tableau-Card-Engine)** — keep the template emitting only what a game repo can actually run.
  - *User story:* "As a core template owner, I want the scaffold to filter core-only scripts (including any future ones) out of generated repos, so a re-scaffold never reintroduces broken entries."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **This repo's `package.json` no longer declares `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games`.** `npm run scaffold` remains and resolves to `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street ...`. Guarded by a regression test (new `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`) asserting the two broken keys are absent and every `scaffold*` script's target file exists.
2. **The scaffold template stops emitting them.** `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` filters the core-only `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` entries out of the inherited scripts map. Add a unit test in `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` whose manifest declares both keys and asserts the rendered `package.json` omits them, so a re-scaffold cannot reintroduce them (AC2 of the original item).
3. **The core change is delivered.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` + its test land in Tableau-Card-Engine (CG work item, per the MS↔CG pairing precedent of MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED↔CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q); this repo records the engine commit via its `./core` submodule pointer bump (`npm run engine:sync`), and `npm run scaffold` on a fixture checkout regenerates a `package.json` without the two keys.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` documents `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo scaffold entry point and states that `scaffold:game(s)` are core-checkout-only commands; no game-repo-context doc references `scaffold:game(s)`. Core docs that use them (DEVELOPER.md, dev/creating-a-new-game.md, dev/multi-repo-architecture.md) are core-checkout context and remain accurate; a one-line "run from the core checkout" clarification is made where ambiguity exists.
5. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (changed-scope test gate plus the added regression tests; core-side suite green in the engine repo). The new `tests/tooling/` file is collected by the existing `unit` project (`tests/**/*.test.ts`, `vite.config.ts:222`) — no project-config change needed.

> **Traceability to the original ACs:** brief AC1 ← original AC1; brief AC2 + AC3 ← original AC2 ("resolve which is true first" resolved: the template emits them by inheritance, so a template filter is required); brief AC4 ← original AC3; brief AC5 ← original AC4.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery** — the template fix lives in the Tableau-Card-Engine repo (`core/` submodule); this item cannot satisfy AC2 in-repo. Push policy applies to both repos: `dev` only.
- **No `npm run scaffold` against the live checkout** — re-scaffolding this repo today **drops 10 locally-added scripts** (`docs`, `docs:build`, `docs:preview`, `pretest`, `test:browser`, `generate:pack-assets`, `validate:storylines`, `storylines:graph:svg`, `docs:diagrams`, `balance:synergy-diversity-report`) because the template does not preserve repo-local extras. AC1 must be done with a hand edit; fixture-based re-scaffold verification lives in tests.
- **No CI beyond npm builds** — the npm build/test scripts are the verification vehicle.
- Implementation follows the mandatory worktree + build→test→commit order of the implement skill; work-item tracking via wl only.

## Existing state

- Issue type stays `chore`: the change removes dead config keys and adjusts the scaffold's config generation; it changes no runtime app behaviour (matches the `discovered-from` item's classification).

- `package.json` (this repo, lines 34–35): `"scaffold:game": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts"`, `"scaffold:games": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all --core-root . --repos-dir .."`. Root `scripts/` contains only `run-tests.ts` and `soak-browser-waits.sh` — the target does not exist.
- `package.json` line 50: `"scaffold": "tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core"` — the working entry point (exists in all sibling repos too).
- `core/package.json` lines 31–32 declare the same two scripts **validly** (core has `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderPackageJson` (lines ~274–312) inherits all core scripts, then overrides repo entry points; `scaffold:game(s)` pass through unchanged.
- 9 sibling game repos (`../tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-f5-verify`, `tce-fresh-verify`, `tce-repos-f9`) carry the same two broken lines — separate repositories, out of scope for this item's ACs (see Follow-ups).
- Related inherited-scripts bug of the same class: 8 more core-only entries arrive broken in every game repo (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — the last breaks `npm run package`/`package:win|linux|mac`). Excluded from scope (see Follow-ups).

## Desired change

1. Remove `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` from this repo's root `package.json` (hand edit; see Constraints).
2. In `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, filter the core-only keys out of the inherited scripts map — a small explicitly-named drop-list (or drop any inherited script that still references the core-only `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` target) with a comment explaining the Option C no-root-`scripts/` rationale and pointing at the follow-up item for the broader class.
3. Add/extend unit tests on both sides; bump the `./core` submodule pointer to the engine commit carrying the template fix.
4. Update `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (and the one-line core-doc clarification in Tableau-Card-Engine).

## Key Files

- `package.json` — remove the two `scaffold:game(s)` entries (this repo).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson`: drop core-only inherited scripts (template fix, engine repo).
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — extend MANIFEST fixture with `scaffold:game(s)` and assert they are omitted from the rendered `package.json`.
- `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts` (new) — regression guard: no `scaffold:game(s)` declared; every `scaffold*` script target exists.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — document `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo entry point; note `scaffold:game(s)` are core-only.
- `.gitmodules` / `gitlink core` — submodule pointer bump to the engine commit with the template fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Dead-key approach is undocumented assumption.** Assumption (recorded, not operator-confirmed): the fix is the narrow one from the item title — drop only `scaffold:game(s)`; the other 8 broken inherited scripts are a separate discovered follow-up (below). If the operator prefers the general filter (fixes all 10), AC1–AC5 grow; flagged, not blocking.
- **R2 — Submodule bump pulls unrelated engine commits.** The engine `dev` head is ahead of the pinned submodule (pinned `9ee194e0…` vs engine `dev` `1c9900a1…`). Mitigation: keep the bump to a reviewable commit; full suite must stay green (AC5).
- **R3 — Incomplete inheritance semantics.** Filtering only `scaffold:game(s)` is a stop-gap while the general class remains broken; over time more core-only scripts may be added. Mitigation: follow-up item tracks the general fix (`discovered-from` link).
- **R4 — Re-scaffold destructiveness discovered during intake.** If the template's preserve-on-re-scaffold behaviour is later expected to keep repo-local scripts, that is a separate enhancement — out of scope here.
- **Scope-creep guard:** sibling-repo clean-up, the 8-script general fix, and template local-script preservation are all recorded as follow-ups, not folded into this item.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** — "[test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts" (the `discovered-from` parent; same scaffold-template class of bug).
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED ↔ CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q** — engine-sync wiring precedent: core template change (in engine repo) + game-repo side + re-scaffold; the MS↔CG pairing model this item follows.
- **CG-0MVGF2QE9008NA5R** — version policy in `renderPackageJson` (the same function being changed).
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** — sibling-repo port of a core template guard; same cross-repo pattern.
- **CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA** — scaffold vite.config template ownership.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** – [test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts (open)
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** – Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version (completed)
- **MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O** – Engine dev tip renamed the story-line docs seam section (game doc-drift test pinned old heading) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mvcrgkzy007died, ac4, appear, banner, broken (+68 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: appear, banner, changes, context, core (+54 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, appear (+50 more)
> Assessment: `MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL` and `MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED` are genuinely related (same template/entry-point class). `MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O` matched on keyword noise (story-line docs seam) and is **not** relevant to this item; repo-file matches are incidental IDF matches. Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0.md`.

## Follow-ups (recorded; out of scope)

- **Generalise the inherited-scripts filter** to all core-only entries that reference the absent game-repo `scripts/` tree (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — `build:electron-main` breakage disables `npm run package*` in every game repo). `discovered-from: MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0`.
- **Re-scaffold sibling game repos** (golf, blackjack, lost-cities, coloretto, feudalism, beleaguered-castle, f5/fresh-verify, repos-f9) or hand-remove the two lines; each is its own repo/worklog item.
- **Template preservation of repo-local scripts** on re-scaffold (R4).

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview was required: the seed context and acceptance criteria were sufficiently defined, and repository search resolved the description's open question ("resolve which is true first") directly:

- Q: Does `renderPackageJson` emit the two broken scripts, or were they hand-copied into game repos? — Answer (agent, repo search): It emits them **by inheritance** — `renderPackageJson` copies the core manifest's whole `scripts` map; `core/package.json` lines 31–32 are the source, and the rendered fixture (core test + node simulation) reproduces both keys. Source: `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (lines ~280–285), `core/package.json` (lines 31–32), `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (MANIFEST/inheritance assertions at lines 293–317), sibling repos `../tce-golf` etc. (same two lines at offset 21–22).
- Q: Can AC1 be satisfied by re-scaffolding this repo? — Answer (agent, simulation): No — re-scaffold would drop 10 locally-added scripts (`docs`, `pretest`, `test:browser`, `generate:pack-assets`, …); AC1 must be a hand edit. Source: node simulation of `renderPackageJson` over the live `core/package.json` vs current root `package.json` (listed in Constraints/Existing state).
- Q: Are the docs that mention `scaffold:game(s)` in game-repo context? — Answer (agent, repo search): No — all three sites (`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md:2075`, `core/docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md:119–123`, `core/docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md:271`) describe core-checkout invocation and stay accurate; they keep the core scripts' validity. This repo's own `docs/` never mentions `scaffold:game(s)`.
