# Wire Bank Loan button into the Turn Summary dialog

Follow-up raised by the Bank Loans planning session (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG), per producer
decision Q4: the Turn Summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) has landed, so its deliberately
disabled **Bank Loan** affordance can now be wired to the loan feature.

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary dialog shows an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** button and never calls
the `onBankLoanAction` seam reserved for the loans feature, so a mid-game player has no
entry point to credit at all — the loan engine only surfaces offers on bankruptcy. This item
turns the reserved affordance into a working mid-game loan entry point, with no new engine
rules.

## Users

- **Mid-game human player (single-player)** — "When the Turn Summary dialog is on screen
  and I am short of cash, I want to borrow from the configured loan menu so I can fund the
  next week's move, and I want to see the repayment schedule before I commit."
- **Cautious player** — "I want the button to tell me *why* it is unavailable (loans turned
  off, or I already owe money) instead of a generic 'coming soon' note."

Not a user of this slice: competitive seats (per-seat closing text, no summary dialog),
AI seats (bailout-only policy — no proactive loans).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Enabled/disabled matrix.** The Bank Loan button is interactive only when
   `state.config.loansEnabled === true` **and** the acting (human) seat holds no active loan;
   in every other case it is rendered disabled (muted, `input` disabled) with a hint that
   explains the reason.
2. **Selector with schedule.** Pressing the enabled button opens the loan selector listing
   every configured `config.loanOptions` entry with its per-turn repayment and total
   repayment, plus a way to back out; backing out returns to the Turn Summary dialog with no
   state change.
3. **Confirm dispatches `takeLoan`.** Confirming an option dispatches the `takeLoan` command
   for the acting seat, credits the principal to that seat's wallet, records the active loan,
   and leaves `actionsRemaining` unchanged.
4. **No day advance.** Neither opening the selector nor confirming a loan advances the day or
   resumes the deferred closing; the day advances only on **[ Next Turn ]**, exactly once.
5. **Refreshed dialog.** After the loan is taken the Turn Summary dialog is re-rendered from
   the same `TurnResult` with the post-`takeLoan` state, so the new obligation is visible and
   the button is now disabled (one-active-loan rule) while **[ Next Turn ]** still works.
6. **Testing/validation.** Tests cover the enabled/disabled matrix (loans enabled + no loan,
   active loan, `loansEnabled: false`), the selector content, the `takeLoan` dispatch, the
   no-action-point rule, the cancel path, and that the day does not advance before
   **[ Next Turn ]**.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments (`showTurnSummaryDialog`, the gate, the button-construction site),
   `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (the "[ Bank Loan ] is always disabled" paragraph), and the
   in-game help/loan documentation touched by MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` renders `[ Bank Loan ]` with `disableInteractive()`, colour
  `#6b6459`, and the hint *“Bank loans are not available yet — coming in a future update.”*;
  it explicitly does `void onBankLoanAction` so the seam can never fire. `BANK_LOAN_HINT` is
  duplicated in `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`, whose AC4 asserts
  "always disabled, seam never invoked" — that test must be rewritten, not deleted.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` delegates to `msOverlayManager`; with no overlay manager (headless) it
  calls `onNextTurn()` immediately so the closing is never stranded.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `shouldGateTurnSummary()` restricts the
  dialog to `requiresDeferredClosing` single-player closings (never replay, reduced motion,
  tutorial or competitive); `presentTurnSummaryGate()` builds the summary with
  `buildTurnSummary(s.state, result)` and calls
  `s.showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn)` — the third argument is not passed today.
- Overlays already read live state (`s.state.config` in `MainStreetOverlayContent`), so
  `loansEnabled` needs no new plumbing into the scene.
- `buildTurnSummary()` is Phaser-free and read-only, so re-rendering after a loan only needs
  the same `state` + `result` pair re-run.
- **The loan engine does not exist yet.** `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `config.loansEnabled`,
  `config.loanOptions`, the `takeLoan` command and `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` are
  all still unimplemented: the Bank Loans epic MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG sits at
  `intake_complete`, its slices are `blocked` (only the headless determinism baseline,
  MS-0MVPWS45N008PR0X, is in flight). This item is the epic's only out-of-epic follow-up and
  must land *after* the model, `takeLoan`, and overlay-UI slices.
- Save schema v3 (loans + pending offer) is delivered by the epic; this slice must not touch
  serialisation.

## Desired change

1. **Carry a loans descriptor into the dialog.** Extend the gate's call so the dialog receives
   one small Phaser-free descriptor rather than reaching into scene state ad hoc — predicted
   shape `{ enabled: boolean; activeLoan: { perTurnRepayment, turnsRemaining } | null;
   options: LoanOption[] }` built in `presentTurnSummaryGate()` from `s.state.config` and the
   acting seat. Keeps the overlay presentation-only and the descriptor unit-testable.
   (Implementation may instead read `s.state` directly if the epic's helpers make that
   cleaner — the ACs do not care which; see Assumptions.)
2. **Enable the affordance** when `enabled && activeLoan === null`, wiring `pointerdown` to
   the `onBankLoanAction` seam; keep the button disabled otherwise with a reason-specific
   hint (loans disabled vs. already owing — see open question Q3).
3. **Loan selector** presented on press: reuse the epic's `MainStreetLoanOverlay` option rows
   (per-turn + total repayment). The epic builds it for a *pending offer* driven by
   `state.pendingLoanOffer`; this slice needs a non-bailout mode (no pending offer, options
   from `config.loanOptions`, Cancel/back instead of Decline). Reusing the row renderer, not
   duplicating it, is the requirement; a small `mode` parameter is expected.
4. **Confirm = dispatch.** Confirming dispatches the `takeLoan` command through the existing
   command surface (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`), never mutating state inline.
5. **Refresh in place** after a successful take: rebuild the summary from the same
   `TurnResult` and re-render the dialog (dismiss the old overlay objects first so
   `s.overlayObjects` stays consistent), leaving `[ Next Turn ]` as the only way to resume
   `advanceTurn`.
6. **Tests** in a new `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` (browser
   overlay, mirroring `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` helpers) plus the rewrite of the
   dialog suite's AC4 case.

## Constraints

- **Presentation wiring only** — no new engine rules, no changes to the loan model, repayment
  maths or one-active-loan validation; those belong to MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
- **No action point cost** and **no day advance** — taking a loan from the dialog must leave
  `actionsRemaining` untouched and must not resume the deferred closing.
- **Single-player deferred path only** — the dialog itself is gated to that path; competitive
  per-seat closing and the tutorial/reduced-motion/replay paths are unchanged.
- **Overlay conventions** (`core` UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` +
  `createOverlayButton`, all elements parented into `s.hudContainer` and pushed to
  `s.overlayObjects`, depths 199/200/201, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), SFX via
  `safePlaySound`.
- **Blocked-by sequencing** — depends on MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (dependency edge already
  recorded): specifically the loan model/config slice (MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB), the `takeLoan`
  command slice (MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79) and the overlay-UI slice (MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA).

## Assumptions

- **A1 First repayment falls on the next turn's closing.** The closing sequence (and its
  ledger) has already run when the dialog is presented, so a loan taken at the dialog must not
  charge a repayment against the turn being summarised. Recorded as OPEN QUESTION Q1 for
  producer confirmation.
- **A2 Proactive loans are allowed at any coin balance** — the button is not gated on
  affordability or negative coins (the goal is mid-game credit, not a second bailout path).
- **A3 The selector's rows come from `config.loanOptions`**, so a re-balanced menu needs no UI
  change, and the dialog is unavailable (button disabled) when the menu is empty.
- **A4 `takeLoan` rejection is surfaced, not swallowed** — if the engine refuses (e.g. a race
  into an active loan), the dialog shows the engine's reason and stays open rather than
  silently closing.
- **A5 Headless safety is untouched** — with no overlay manager the scene still calls
  `onNextTurn()`; the new descriptor must remain optional so existing call sites compile.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Sequencing risk (highest):** the epic is not implemented; starting this slice early would
  mean inventing engine helpers (scope creep). Mitigation: keep the item dependency-blocked
  until the three prerequisites are `completed`.
- **Duplicated overlay logic:** copy-pasting the bailout overlay instead of parameterising it
  would leave two loan selectors to maintain. Mitigation: AC2/desired-change 3 require reusing
  the epic's row renderer.
- **Stale dialog content:** re-rendering from a mutated `state` but a stale `TurnResult` can
  show a mismatch. Mitigation: rebuild via `buildTurnSummary(state, result)` with the same
  `result` object (the ledger is presentation data, not recomputed).
- **Overlay object leak:** dismissing and re-rendering must reset `s.overlayObjects` the same
  way `dismissOverlay` does, or duplicated buttons accumulate in `hudContainer`. Mitigation:
  explicit test asserting a single `[ Next Turn ]`/`[ Bank Loan ]` pair after a refresh.
- **Test drift:** `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` AC4 encodes "always disabled"; leaving
  it untouched makes the suite self-contradictory. Mitigation: rewrite that case in the same
  commit.
- **Scope creep:** competitive-mode parity (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI), AI proactive loans, multiple
  loans, loan repayment UI polish — record as linked work items, do not fold in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — enable/disable `[ Bank Loan ]`, wire the seam,
  render the reason-specific hint and refresh the dialog after a take.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — build and pass the loans descriptor in
  `presentTurnSummaryGate()`; keep `shouldGateTurnSummary()` unchanged.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — pass the descriptor through the delegation method.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — reuse the epic's option rows in a non-bailout
  (mid-game select) mode.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — consume `activeLoanFor` / option-table helpers (read-only use).
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoan` command dispatch and the no-AP assertion.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` — **new.** Wiring tests.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` — rewrite the "seam never invoked"
  case.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — update the "always disabled" Turn Summary paragraph.

## Out of scope / non-goals

- Competitive-mode summary dialog and any competitive loan entry point
  (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI).
- Engine rules: repayment timing, bailout offer loop, AI policy, persistence — owned by
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
- HUD obligation readout (MS-0MVPWSCRD004A6Z4) and the loans help/documentation slice
  (MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB); this item only edits the one doc paragraph it invalidates.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** (Bank Loans, epic, `intake_complete`) — the engine this slice wires
  into; dependency edge recorded.
- **MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB** (Loan model, config and repayment maths), **MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79**
  (`takeLoan` command and one-active-loan rule), **MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA** (Bailout overlay UI
  and deferred closing resume) — prerequisites.
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (End of Turn summary, completed) — parent of the dialog; its AC
  anticipated the Bank Loan button.
- **MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT** (Overlay: turn summary dialog + browser test, completed) — created
  the disabled affordance and its `onBankLoanAction` seam.
- **MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R** (deferred closing gate, completed) — the gate that presents the
  dialog; see `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate".
- **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI** (End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode, open) — the other
  mode's dialog; explicitly not covered here.
- Repo: `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`,
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (repayment timing): "A loan taken from the Turn Summary dialog — when does the first
  repayment hit? (A) at the next turn's closing, since this turn's closing and ledger have
  already run [recommended]; (B) immediately when the deferred closing resumes, so the turn
  just summarised carries it; (C) other." — **OPEN QUESTION.** No answer yet; the item is
  blocked by the epic anyway. Draft assumes **A** (see Assumption A1). Source: raised in the
  intake session 2026-10-27, no interactive producer available (auto-dispatched downtime run).
- Q2 (mode scope): "Should the enabled button also cover any non-single-player summary
  surface? (A) no — single-player deferred path only; competitive parity stays with
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI [recommended]; (B) cover competitive too." — **OPEN QUESTION**, draft
  assumes **A** (already consistent with `shouldGateTurnSummary`).
- Q3 (disabled hint wording): "When the seat already holds an active loan, what should the
  disabled hint say? (A) show the outstanding obligation, e.g. *'Active loan: 110 coins/week,
  4 weeks left.'* [recommended]; (B) a generic *'You already have an active loan.'*; (C) keep
  the current generic text." — **OPEN QUESTION**, draft assumes **A**.
- Q4 (proactive eligibility): "Is the button available at any balance, or only when the seat
  cannot cover its costs?" — answered from the seed goal (mid-game credit use case): **any
  balance**, recorded as Assumption A2. Source: work-item description "As a mid-game player …
  I can click [ Bank Loan ]".
- Q5 (selector reuse): "Does the epic's bailout overlay support a non-bailout option list?" —
  research: `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` does not exist yet; the epic's Key Files
  predict it as the pending-offer overlay. Draft therefore requires a reuse with a mode
  parameter rather than a copy (Risks: duplicated overlay logic). Source: `wl show
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG --json`, `ls src/scenes/`.
- Q6 (dependency): "Is the loan engine available to wire against?" — research: no — `grep -ri
  loan src` returns only the dialog's placeholder comments; the epic is at `intake_complete`
  with its slices `blocked`. Recorded as a hard prerequisite. Source: repo grep, `wl search
  loan --json`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT** – Overlay: turn summary dialog + browser test (completed)
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary. When all animations for the End of Turn phase have completed we should pop up a dialog with details of the current state of the game. # of businesses owned by each player, income and expenses for that turn, one-off income/expenses (from events etc.) and any other information that would be useful and informative. The dialog will have a "next turn" button and a "Bank Loan" button which will allow them to take out a loan (a feature not yet implemented, see work item) (completed)
- **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI** – End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (open)

# Add wall-clock bounded-deferral helper with contract tests

## Headline

Add the shared injectable bounded-deferral helper (wall-clock deadline + wall-clock `setTimeout` re-poll, forced completion at `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`, no-clock degradation, stale-scene guard) together with its contract tests — tests written first, tree green at close. Verified end-to-end: unit tests prove wall-clock enforcement, hidden-tab semantics, injectability and single cap source.

## Summary

Implements the parent's decision C: the helper computes its deadline from `Date.now()`, re-polls with `window.setTimeout` (not the scene clock), forces completion after `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time, enforces the cap even when the page is not painting (Q2 = 1), degrades to immediate continuation where no clock/timer exists, and exposes its clock/timer for deterministic unit driving. No deferral site is adopted here (adoption is the next child, keeping the change reviewable); production pacing constants are untouched.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — helper added sibling to `scheduleOrRun` (~line 176) and exported.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` unchanged; comment updated to the wall-clock contract.
- `tests/main-street/bounded-deferral.test.ts` — new contract tests (written before the helper, green at close).
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` — the cap-location pin migrates to the helper extraction.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — pass unmodified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Helper has a wall-clock deadline (`Date.now()`-derived) and a wall-clock re-poll (`window.setTimeout`) and forces the continuation (clears `incomeCollectionActive`, invokes the caller continuation) once `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time elapses.
- [ ] A unit test with a **frozen scene clock and an advancing wall clock** proves the continuation is forced within one poll interval of the 16 000 ms cap.
- [ ] Injectable clock/timer parameters (defaulting to `Date.now`/`setTimeout`); a unit test proves **no-clock degradation** (headless scene runs the continuation immediately, preserving `scheduleOrRun` semantics); a unit test proves a **stale wall timer never fires into a destroyed scene** (`scene.isActive()` guard + try-catch).
- [ ] `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` pin migrated to assert the **helper consumes** `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` and no inline `startAt = <scene clock> + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` / `delayedCall(250, <poll>)` poll site remains in either module — the duplication cannot silently return.
- [ ] `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays 16 000 as the only cap value; `MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` comment states the wall-clock enforcement contract.
- [ ] Unit project green (`/skill:test --type unit`); existing fake-clock suites (`competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`, `turnflow.test.ts`) pass unmodified (no weakened assertions).
- [ ] One bounded-deferral helper, wall-clock enforced (all poll sites).
- [ ] Forced advance is not tied to paint: wall timer drives the cap while the document is hidden.
- [ ] Injectable and backward-compatible: the helper accepts an injectable clock/timer and preserves no-clock degradation.
- [ ] Single source of truth for the cap: `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays the only cap value.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the contract tests first (frozen clock + advancing wall clock; hidden document; no-clock; stale scene) against the intended public API.
2. Add the helper next to `scheduleOrRun` with injectable `now`/`schedule` parameters defaulting to wall clock; enforce the stale-scene guard; document the wall-clock contract in the module comment.
3. Migrate the cap-location pin in `income-collection-cap.test.ts`; update the `MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` comment.
4. Run the unit profile: all green, existing suites unaffected.

# Transient feedback toasts: readable hold, animate/pause/fade, always on top

**Headline:** Main Street's transient feedback toast (the channel that explains an illegal move, e.g. "Not enough coins to place Bakery") is currently a single 1.1 s pop that starts fading immediately and renders at depth 0, inside the hand band — so it cannot be read and is covered by hand cards. Make it a proper toast: fade/pop in, hold fully opaque for 0.5 s per word, fade out, render above every other scene element, and clear the hand band.

## Problem statement

When a move is refused, the player gets an explanation through `flashError()` → `flashFeedback()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts`). The message is created by `popTextOrIcon` with a 1.1 s total lifetime, a fade that begins on the first frame, depth 0, and an anchor at `handY − 20` — which is inside the hand-card row (cards are centred on `handY`, so the top of the cards is `handY − handCardH/2`). The result is text that is too fast to read and is covered by the hand and higher-depth HUD/overlay layers.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "When I make an illegal move, I want to read *why* it was refused without racing the fade or the hand, so I can correct my move instead of guessing."
- **Reduced-motion player:** "I still need the same explanation held for the same readable time, without animation."
- **QA/designer:** "I want the toast's timing and layer to be deterministic and assertable, so a regression is caught by the suite rather than by playing the game."
- **Developer:** "I want one place that owns toast presentation so the feedback channel stays consistent as more messages move into it."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Word-based readable hold.** A pure helper (e.g. `feedbackHoldMs(text)`) derives the fully-opaque hold from the message's whitespace-delimited word count: `words × 500 ms` (minimum one word's 500 ms). The toast stays at alpha 1 for exactly that hold between fade-in and fade-out; a 5-word refusal is readable for 2.5 s, not 1.1 s total. Unit tests cover 1, 5 and 10-word messages and empty text.
- [ ] **AC2 — Animate → pause → fade.** Normal presentation runs fade/scale-in (~160 ms), the AC1 fully-opaque pause, then fade-out (~300 ms) before destruction; total lifetime is `fadeIn + hold + fadeOut`. No fade or motion occurs during the pause. Under reduced motion the toast is static at alpha 1 for the same AC1 hold and is then destroyed — no tweens, never dropped. Unit tests assert the sequence, that alpha stays 1 through the hold, and that reduced motion creates no tween.
- [ ] **AC3 — Always above, clear of the hand.** Both the animated and reduced-motion toasts render at a named depth above every Main Street layer (hand cards 0…n, hand panel −100, action row 100, overlays 200–201, stats 900–950, HUD 1000, stats button 1100), e.g. `FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH = 3000`. The anchor is lifted clear of the hand-card band (`handY − handCardH/2 − margin`) using layout values, with a safe fallback when metrics are missing. Tests assert the applied depth and anchor with the real layout shape.
- [ ] **AC4 — One readable toast, wrapped.** Only one feedback toast is live per scene: a new message destroys the previous toast, cancels its hold/dismiss timers and starts fresh (no stacked duplicates at the same anchor). Long messages word-wrap within the viewport (max width derived from `gameW`) and carry a dark stroke so they stay legible over any background. Tests cover replacement/cancellation and wrap-width selection.
- [ ] **AC5 — Existing feedback contract unchanged.** Message taxonomy (error/confirmation surfaced; guidance/progress dropped), `scene.lastFeedback` / `scene.feedbackHistory`, Activity Log behaviour and the `flashError`/`flashConfirmation` API remain unchanged; the toast is never interactive and never intercepts pointer input. Existing feedback/illegal-afford tests stay green (anchor expectations updated only for the deliberate lift).
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README where relevant, and the VitePress pages under `docs/` (in particular `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Transient pop-text feedback channel*).
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **In-repo only.** Implement in `src/scenes/` (Main Street). Do **not** edit the engine-owned `core/` submodule or bump the engine pin; the engine's `illegalMoveToast` is a separate component and is not composed by Main Street at this pin.
- **Reduced motion is mandatory.** The in-game setting / `prefers-reduced-motion` path must remain animation-free while preserving the same hold time.
- **No input capture.** The toast is presentation-only; do not make it interactive.
- **Deterministic and testable.** Drive timing through Phaser time/tweens (or an injected clock in tests), never fixed real-time sleeps.
- **Base layout is 1280×720 but expands.** Use layout values (`handY`, `handCardH`, `gameW`, `logX`) rather than new hard-coded pixel positions.
- **Scope is feedback toasts.** Animation-only `popTextOrIcon` effects (income counters, level-up, card-transfer VFX) keep their current short pop; word-based dwell would stall their animation sequences.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline). Do not add CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts`:
  - `flashFeedback()` records `scene.lastFeedback` / `feedbackHistory`, then uses `duration = options.duration ?? 1100`.
  - Normal path calls `popTextOrIcon({ scene, x, y, label, duration: 1100, riseY: 20, scale: 1.1, reducedMotion: false })`.
  - Reduced-motion path creates `scene.add.text(...).setOrigin(0.5).setDepth(900)` and destroys it after `duration`.
  - `feedbackAnchor(layout)` returns `{ x: logX / 2, y: handY − 20 }`.
- `popTextOrIcon` (`@ui/popTextOrIcon`, engine-owned) runs one tween for the whole duration: `y −20`, `alpha → 0`, `scale 1.1`. There is no pause, and the text has no explicit depth (defaults to 0) or wrap width.
- Depth landscape: hand cards use `depth = index` (0…n), hand panel `−100`, action row `100`, overlays `200–201`, stats `900–950`, HUD `1000`, stats button `1100`. A depth-0 toast therefore sits under hand cards and every HUD/overlay layer.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/feedback-pop-text.test.ts` mocks `popTextOrIcon` and asserts anchor `{ x: 410, y: 600 }` for `{ logX: 820, handY: 620 }`, plus the reduced-motion static path. `tests/main-street/illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` asserts `scene.lastFeedback` text for refusals.
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` documents the current 1100 ms `popTextOrIcon` presentation.

## Desired change

1. **Pure timing helper:** `feedbackHoldMs(text: string): number` → `max(1, wordCount) × 500` ms; empty/whitespace text returns 0 (no toast). Export it for tests.
2. **Toast presentation in `MainStreetFeedback`:** create the text at the anchor with `FONT_FAMILY` and the existing 18 px bold white style, origin 0.5, `setDepth(FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH)`, `setWordWrapWidth(min(FEEDBACK_TOAST_MAX_WIDTH, gameW − 40))`, dark stroke, alpha 0/scale 0.9. Fade/scale in over `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_IN_MS`, hold for `feedbackHoldMs(text)`, fade out over `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_OUT_MS`, then destroy. Reduced motion: alpha 1, no tweens, destroy after the hold.
3. **Replacement:** keep at most one toast per scene (module `WeakMap` or a scene field); on a new message, cancel the previous hold timer/tweens and destroy the previous text before showing the new one. Bind scene shutdown/destroy cleanup so no timer or text leaks.
4. **Anchor:** `feedbackAnchor` gains the hand-card height (optional for backward compatibility) and returns `y = handY − handCardH/2 − FEEDBACK_TOAST_MARGIN_PX`; keep the current `logX / 2` horizontal centring and the safe fallback when layout metrics are missing.
5. **Constants:** add `FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_IN_MS`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_OUT_MS`, `FEEDBACK_WORD_HOLD_MS = 500`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_MARGIN_PX`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_MAX_WIDTH` to `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` (or a small local block if that file is not the right home).
6. **Tests:** rework `tests/main-street/feedback-pop-text.test.ts` to assert `feedbackHoldMs`, the fade→hold→fade sequence with a fake scene, alpha 1 during the hold, depth/wrap/anchor, replacement/cancellation, reduced motion with no tweens, and unchanged classification/history. Keep `illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` green.
7. **Docs:** update `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Transient pop-text feedback channel* (hold formula, sequence, depth, anchor, replacement, reduced motion).

**Order of work (test-first):** write the new timing/presentation tests against the agreed contract, then the helper and constants, then the presentation/replacement and anchor lift, then the docs.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts` — New helper, toast presentation/replacement, anchor lift, reduced-motion path.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — New toast depth, fade/hold/margin/wrap constants if not kept local to the feedback module.
- `tests/main-street/feedback-pop-text.test.ts` — Reworked timing, depth, anchor, replacement and reduced-motion tests.
- `tests/main-street/illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` — Regression: illegal-move reasons still surface through `lastFeedback`.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Update the transient feedback channel presentation contract.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVPWQK3U003DIR6** (completed, `in_review`) — *[Impl] Remove instruction line and route feedback to pop text*: introduced `MainStreetFeedback`, `feedbackAnchor`, `lastFeedback`/`feedbackHistory`, and the 1100 ms `popTextOrIcon` presentation this item replaces.
- **MS-0MVKTB6WS000VLWK** (completed, `in_review`) — *UI simplification when roads are visible*: parent decision that errors/confirmations are surfaced as transient pop text and guidance/progress are dropped (Q4a). This item keeps that taxonomy.
- **CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB** (engine, completed) — *Core illegal-move routine: explain a rejected move with a reason toast*: adds an engine-side `illegalMoveToast` (dwell 2500 ms, depth 1900, y 520). It is **not** composed by Main Street at the pinned engine `0409c1eb`, and `playIllegalFeedback()` does not pass a `reason`; Main Street's visible illegal-move explanation is the `flashError` toast. If the producer intended that engine toast instead, this item must be re-scoped to `~/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine` plus a Main Street re-pin.
- **MS-0MVQO6N34007DHP8** (critical) — *Bumping the engine pin to core dev tip breaks the unit suite (`phaser window is not defined`)*: relevant only if scope is later widened to the engine toast; it does not block the in-repo feedback toast fix.
- **Docs:** `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Transient pop-text feedback channel*; `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (illegal feedback description).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — observed toast is the Main Street feedback channel.** At the pinned engine `0409c1eb`, `shakeIllegalMove` has no `reason` toast and `playIllegalFeedback` passes no reason, so the illegal-move reason the player sees is `flashError` → `flashFeedback` (1100 ms, depth 0, inside the hand band). This exactly matches the report. Research: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts:62`, `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts:88`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts:20-64`, `core` gitlink `0409c1eb`.
- **Assumption — scope is feedback toasts only.** `popTextOrIcon` is also used directly for short animation VFX (income `+€`, level-up, card transfer). Those are markers, not explanations; applying a word-based hold would stall animation sequences and is out of scope.
- **Risk — scope creep into the engine toast.** The engine's shared `illegalMoveToast` has the same readability problem (fixed 2500 ms dwell, y 520, depth 1900). It is deliberately not bundled here; record it as a separate engine item and a re-pin if the producer wants it.
- **Risk — long messages linger.** A 20-word reason holds for 10 s. This is the producer's explicit 0.5 s/word rule; the toast is non-interactive and can be replaced by the next message, so it does not block play. No cap is added unless the producer asks for one.
- **Risk — depth above overlays.** `FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH = 3000` puts the toast above the stats/help overlays and the HUD. A toast raised while a modal is open will sit over the modal for its bounded lifetime; replacement and auto-dismiss keep that window short. The producer explicitly asked for "above all other elements".
- **Risk — regression in tests pinned to the old anchor.** `feedback-pop-text.test.ts` asserts `y: 600`; the deliberate lift changes that to `handY − handCardH/2 − margin`. Update the assertions with the new contract, do not weaken them.
- **Risk — leaked timers/tweens.** Replacement and scene shutdown must cancel pending hold/fade timers and destroy the text; tests use fake time to prove no callbacks fire after replacement.
- **Assumption — no background panel.** Legibility is achieved with a dark stroke over the text rather than a filled chip; the producer asked for animate/pause/fade/on-top, not a panel. A chip can be added later if the stroke is not enough.
- **Assumption — `duration` option.** No call site passes `FeedbackOptions.duration`; its role is replaced by the word-based hold. To avoid a silent breaking change, keep an optional explicit hold override (renamed `holdMs`) for tests/back-compat and default it to `feedbackHoldMs(text)`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was required: the seed context (too fast, animate/pause/fade, 0.5 s per word, above all elements) plus repository investigation resolved the scope and contract. Each resolution is recorded for producer review.

- Q: "Which toast is the report about — Main Street's feedback pop text or the engine's `illegalMoveToast`?" — Answer (agent, repository investigation): **Main Street's feedback pop text**. Research: the pinned engine is `0409c1eb`, before the engine reason-toast commit `34e0ab6d`; `playIllegalFeedback()` calls `shakeIllegalMove` without a `reason`, so no engine toast is rendered in Main Street. The illegal-move reason is surfaced by `flashError()` (`MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts:62`) through `flashFeedback` → `popTextOrIcon` at 1100 ms, depth 0, anchor `handY − 20` (inside the hand band). Source: `git -C core log --all -- src/ui/illegalMoveToast.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts`.
- Q: "Does 'toasts' include every `popTextOrIcon` call, e.g. income and level-up numbers?" — Answer (agent): **No — feedback toasts only** (`flashFeedback`/`flashError`/`flashConfirmation`). Research: direct `popTextOrIcon` calls are animation VFX with short, self-explanatory labels and are sequenced with board animations; a word-based hold would stall them. Source: `grep -rn popTextOrIcon src/scenes`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Event Feedback Animations*.
- Q: "What exactly should 'animate, pause, fade' mean, and how is the 0.5 s/word pause applied?" — Answer (agent): **fade/scale-in ~160 ms → fully opaque hold of `words × 500 ms` → fade-out ~300 ms**; total lifetime is the sum. Reduced motion skips the tweens but keeps the same hold. Source: producer's seed description; implemented contract in AC1/AC2.
- Q: "What does 'above all other elements' mean for layer depth?" — Answer (agent): **a named depth above every Main Street layer** (`FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH = 3000`, above hand cards 0…n, hand panel −100, action 100, overlays 200–201, stats 900–950, HUD 1000, stats button 1100), plus an anchor lifted clear of the hand-card band. Source: `grep -rn setDepth src/scenes core/src/ui/HandView.ts`, `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` hand-panel geometry.
- Q: "Should a new message stack with the previous toast or replace it?" — Answer (agent): **replace**. Research: repeated refusals currently create multiple overlapping `popTextOrIcon` texts at the same anchor; one live toast is the readable and testable contract. Source: `MainStreetFeedback.flashFeedback` current create-per-call behaviour; engine `illegalMoveToast` precedent (single live toast per scene).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVKTB6WS000VLWK** – UI simplification when roads are visible (completed)
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** – Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed)
- **MS-0MVPWQO3B008B574** – [Docs] Document opaque panels, hand anchor and hint removal (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac4, ac5, acceptance, action, activity (+443 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: 0mvpwqk3u003dir6, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+394 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, action, add, added, adds (+363 more)

# Intake Brief: Park should give a good reputation bonus

**Work item:** MS-0MVRDGNFU001DDQW · `feature` · `medium`
**Status:** Producer answers recorded (2026-10-28): **+20 reputation/turn, pricing maintained (150 / 40)** — ready for planning.

## Headline

The Park (`cs-park`) is the **only community space that yields no reputation per
turn**, while carrying the **highest running cost in the game** (40 coins/turn)
— it produces neither income nor reputation and the balance analysis records it
as a net drain. Give it the producer-confirmed **+20 reputation/turn**, keeping
its cost 150 and 40/turn running cost unchanged, restoring it as an attractive
tier-1 Entertainment anchor and the cheapest reputation entry in the game.

## Problem statement

The Park currently provides no value to the player. All seven other community
spaces generate `reputationPerTurn` (Playground 20, Garden 40, Fountain 40,
Library 40, Health Kiosk 60, Shelter 60, Public Art 80); the Park has an empty
`reputationPerTurn` (0) while costing 40 coins/turn to run — the highest
`ongoingCost` of any community space. `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md`
records it as a "pure net drain" (remedied by re-pricing 300 → 150 in
MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5, but the zero reputation remained). The producer decision
(2026-10-28) sets **+20 reputation/turn** with pricing kept at 150/40.

## Users

- **Player** — building an Entertainment cluster should feel rewarded: the Park
  is a tier-1, tutorial-visible card that currently reads as a money pit.
  *"As a player, I want the Park to grow my reputation, so that placing it is a
  strategic choice rather than an obvious mistake."*
- **Producer / balance owner** — confirmed the value and pricing on
  2026-10-28; wants the guardrails verified and the docs updated to match.
- **Developer** — a single-row, data-only change: the machinery that applies
  `reputationPerTurn` (per-turn income, tooltips, AI scoring) already exists and
  needs no engine changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-park` in `src/card-data.csv` gains `reputationPerTurn = 20`
   (producer-confirmed 2026-10-28; integer, no cost or `ongoingCost` change —
   remains 150 and 40). The description is updated with the existing wording
   convention used by Library/Garden/Fountain ("Provides +20 reputation per
   turn."), and the `card-text-data-consistency` test passes.
2. **Value visible automatically** — the Park's card tooltip shows the +20
   rep/turn line, the per-turn reputation total includes it (existing
   `MainStreetEngineCommands` path), and UI/AI scoring that reads
   `reputationPerTurn` reflect the new value with no engine change.
3. **Retune-contract baseline updated deliberately** —
   `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts` pins `cs-park: 0`
   (`PRE_RETUNE_COMMUNITY_SPACE_REP`). This is the only card whose value
   changes outside the ×4 retune (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE), so the baseline entry
   and the test's rationale comment are updated with a pointer to this item
   (a deliberate, documented contract change, not a silent regression).
4. **Balance sanity** — the Monte Carlo / tutorial guardrails remain within
   band after the change (Park now contributes +20 passive reputation and looks
   more attractive to the AI's community-space scoring); any drift is measured
   and reported, and no band is silently widened.
5. **Documentation updated** — `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (Park row and its
   rationale line about "zero reputation and negative net value"),
   `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` (community-space table), and
   any other doc listing Park's rep/turn (e.g.
   `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` note) are updated to
   the confirmed +20 value.
6. **Regeneration** — CSV-derived static SVGs/checksum
   (`public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json`) are
   regenerated; card face text reflects the new description.
7. **Full project test suite passes with the new changes** (including any
   existing tests that assert Park has no reputation, e.g.
   `tests/main-street/card-diagrams.test.ts` Park detail).

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** reputation per turn must be a whole number (20).
- **Balance levers only:** changes are limited to `card-data.csv`
   (`reputationPerTurn`) and description/docs; **no cost/ongoingCost change**
   (producer decision Q2 = maintain 150 / 40) and no engine-rule changes.
   Values are data-is-source-of-truth.
- **Do not break the win-rate ladder** `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard` (primary balance
   gate).
- **No new cards, no scope creep:** `upg-garden` (Park → Garden upgrade),
   other card values, and AI heuristic changes are out of scope.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv` `cs-park`: cost **150**, `baseIncome` 0, Entertainment,
  `ongoingCost` **40**, `reputationPerTurn` empty (0). Description: "Offers
  leisure space. Gains {SYNERGY_RATE} of base income per adjacent Entertainment
  business or community space. Costs 40 coins per turn to run."
- Current community-space reputation set (post-×4 retune,
  MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE): Playground 20 (300/ongoing 20), Garden 40 (350/10),
  Fountain 40 (350/25), Library 40 (400/25), Health Kiosk 60 (450/15),
  Shelter 60 (400/30), Public Art 80 (600/25). Park is the outlier at 0.
- Confirmed target (+20 rep, 150/40): rep per 100 coins of cost = 13.3 — inside
  the community-space band (Playground 6.7 … Shelter 15; Public Art/Kiosk 13.3),
  and still net-negative in coin-equivalent (−10 coins/turn at the documented
  1.5 coins/rep) — a deliberate producer choice: the Park is a cheap
  reputation-first card with the game's highest upkeep, not a coin earner.
- Test contracts that pin current Park values:
  `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts:66` (`'cs-park': 0`),
  `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` (Park tooltip),
  `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts:259`, `card-diagrams.test.ts`
  (Park detail), `community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (Park fixtures).

## Desired change

1. Set `cs-park.reputationPerTurn = 20` in `src/card-data.csv` and update the
   card description to state "Provides +20 reputation per turn." in the
   existing wording convention.
2. Keep `cost` 150 and `ongoingCost` 40 (producer decision Q2).
3. Update the docs tables and the retune-contract test baseline (deliberate
   change), and regenerate the CSV-derived card artefacts.

**Key Files:**

- `src/card-data.csv` — `cs-park` row: `reputationPerTurn` + description text.
- `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts` — `'cs-park': 0`
  baseline + rationale comment (deliberate contract change).
- `tests/main-street/card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — enforces
  data/description agreement for the "+20 reputation per turn" wording.
- `tests/main-street/card-diagrams.test.ts` — Park diagram detail test.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` — Park tooltip assertion.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` —
  Park fixtures/expectations may shift as AI now scores its reputation.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — Park cash-line fixture.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — Park
  ongoing-cost fixtures.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` — balance gate
  evidencing the change (drift measured, not silently widened).
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — regenerates the
  CSV-derived SVG/checksum artefacts.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — Park row and its rationale line.
- `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` — community-space table.
- `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` — repricing note.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** — Re-tune reputation sources (×4 retune) — left
  Park at 0 deliberately; the contract test that must be updated lives here.
- **MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5** — Re-price community spaces — set Park cost 150
  "to reflect its zero reputation and negative net value"; this item removes
  that premise.
- **MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL** — Per-turn running costs for Playground/Fountain/
  Shelter — established the producer-owned-value AC pattern and the
  description wording "Provides +N reputation per turn."
- **CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK** — Park 40/turn running cost (precedent).
- **CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE / CG-0MSKS963N000ZSTU** — Park-model synergy
  participation (unchanged by this item).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no engine change is required — `reputationPerTurn` already
  flows into per-turn reputation (`MainStreetEngineCommands`), tooltips,
  diagram detail and AI scoring, all derived from CSV. Verified by source scan.
- **Balance drift:** giving Park +20 reputation changes AI placement desirability
  and the passive-reputation economy; run the guardrails and report drift
  rather than widening bands (per the drift-report-then-ask workflow).
- **Value-by-design:** at +20 the Park stays net-negative in coin-equivalent
  (−10/turn) — the producer's deliberate choice of a reputation-first card with
  the highest upkeep; the AC4 balance gate confirms the ladder is unaffected.
- **Contract-test coupling:** the ×4-retune contract deliberately pins
  `cs-park: 0`; updating it is expected but must be deliberate and documented
  (AC3), otherwise a reviewer will read it as a regression.
- **Scope creep:** upgrade-card economics (`upg-garden`), AI heuristics, and
  the other seven community spaces are out of scope; record as linked items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: What reputation-per-turn should the Park provide? — **Answer (producer,
  2026-10-28): +20.** The intake recommendation was +40 (parity with
  Library/Garden/Fountain; the first value making the Park net-positive in
  coin-equivalent), and the producer chose the lower +20 instead. Accepted
  value: 20. Rationale the +20 choice is coherent: 20/150 cost gives 13.3 rep
  per 100 coins — inside the community-space band (Playground 6.7, Library 10,
  Kiosk/Public Art 13.3) — and the Park stays a cheap, reputation-first tier-1
  card whose high 40/turn upkeep is its built-in anti-spam lever. Source:
  interactive producer reply; evidence: `src/card-data.csv` community-space
  rows, `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md`, MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE,
  MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5.
- Q2: Keep cost 150 / ongoing 40, or re-price? — **Answer (producer,
  2026-10-28): maintain 150 / 40.** Accepted: pricing unchanged; only the
  `reputationPerTurn` value changes in AC1. Preserves the MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5
  repricing intent and the CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK running-cost precedent.
- Q3 (answered, agent): Description wording? — Use the shipped convention
  ("Provides +N reputation per turn.") matching Library/Garden/Fountain, since
  `card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` enforces data/text agreement. Source:
  existing `card-data.csv` descriptions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV8LHN0W0017XU1** – Reputation bonuses should have no delay between businesses (completed)
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** – Visual representation of reputation (completed)
- **MS-0MV8LHN5U008B9JJ** – AI staff should not give players bonuses (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` — matched: bonus, currently, give, good, park (+6 more)
- `core/docs/the-build/concept-evaluation.md` — matched: bonus, give, good, park, player (+5 more)
- `docs/dev/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: bonus, currently, give, good, player (+5 more)

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-29 — plan (auto-complete path, effort Small / risk Medium).**
  Leaf `feature` with measurable ACs, a minimal implementation sketch, and
  producer answers already recorded at intake (Q1 +20 rep/turn, Q2 maintain
  150/40) — no decomposition needed and no child work items created. The item
  is a single small vertical slice spanning data, tests, docs and artefact
  regeneration; phasing was considered and rejected because every AC verifies
  the same one-row change.

  Six automated review stages ran against the existing content:
  - **Requirements & AC alignment** — all 7 ACs trace to the brief's
    requirements; AC1 reflects the producer's +20 and unchanged 150/40; no
    invented or contradictory criteria.
  - **Completeness** — normalised the Key Files heading to the machine-readable
    `**Key Files:**` form, split the combined docs bullet into one path per
    bullet, and added the missing verification files
    (`card-text-data-consistency.test.ts`, `cash-line-overlay.test.ts`,

# Competitive Turn Summary row end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

Competitive play gains the same review-and-advance moment single-player already
has: after the shared day's closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary
panel shows one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat, and the next shared
day starts only when the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**.

This is the tracer bullet slice: it cuts through **every** layer (engine ledger
→ Phaser-free model → overlay → scene gate) with the smallest useful row set
(businesses owned, per-phase income, net coin change), so the wire-up is
demonstrable end-to-end before later slices thicken the columns.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `TurnResult` gains an optional owner-keyed competitive round ledger (e.g. `playerRoundLedger?: OwnerRoundLedger[]`, or an optional per-owner field added to `OwnerIncomeResult`) exposing, per non-eliminated seat and in seat order: `businessesOwned`, the per-phase income subtotal, and `netCoinChange`. The field is optional and absent-safe: single-player, N=1 and headless callers are unchanged when it is absent.
2. `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` populates the ledger for N ≥ 2 (threaded through `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`, including the deferred dual-choice resume) without changing the coins deducted or credited, the shared phase order (Income → Incident → EndCheck), RNG consumption, or the emitted log lines.
3. `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` builds one owner-keyed competitive row per seat the closing surfaced, reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard` labels (`You` / `AI n`) and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours; it returns `null` when the result carries no competitive ledger, so single-player and browser callers are unaffected.
4. In the animations-enabled competitive closing path the panel appears after `presentCompetitiveClosing` completes, and `startTurnPhase` runs only on **[ Next Turn ]** — the next shared day does not advance before the click.
5. The panel renders **[ Next Turn ]** (primary, SFX via `safePlaySound`) and an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** with the explanatory hint, behind an `onBankLoanAction` seam shaped so MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG can make it per-seat (`(seatId?: number) => void`) without re-plumbing. Reduced motion, replay and headless keep today's auto-advance pacing.
6. Parent criterion delivered — In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing. This slice delivers the businesses-owned, per-phase income and net-change columns; the ongoing-expense and closing-balance columns land in the dependent slices.
7. Parent criterion delivered — The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.

## Test-first checklist

Write these tests before the implementation edits (TDD within the slice):

- **Engine** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` — per-owner ledger values for a 2-seat and a 3-seat engine run; eliminated seat omitted; no ledger on N=1 / single-player; each seat's committed `PlayerRecord` coins identical to the ledger-less baseline.
- **Model** `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` — one row per seat, seat order, `You` / `AI n` labels and seat colours, per-row businesses owned / income / net; `null` when the competitive ledger is absent.
- **Gate** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — panel presented after the closing; `startTurnPhase` not called before **[ Next Turn ]** and called exactly once after; reduced-motion / replay / headless advance immediately.

## Minimal implementation

1. Declare the optional ledger types/fields in `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` (next to `TurnLedger` / `OwnerIncomeResult`) and re-export from `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts`.
2. Capture the values in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` where `playerIncome` is already produced, and carry them through `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`.
3. Add a competitive-row builder in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` (extend `buildTurnSummary` or add `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary`) using the scoreboard label/colour conventions.
4. Extend `showTurnSummaryDialog` (or add a thin competitive sibling sharing the same panel) in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` to render one row per owner, keeping the existing single-player call site working; delegate from `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`.
5. Gate the competitive tail in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`) with a `shouldGateCompetitiveTurnSummary` / `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` pair mirroring the single-player gate in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`

## Reuse (do not rebuild)

- The single-player panel, model and gate (`buildTurnSummary`, `showTurnSummaryDialog`, `shouldGateTurnSummary` / `presentTurnSummaryGate`) — extend, don't fork, so both modes share one presentation.

## Deliverables

## Goal

expense detail. Per-seat ongoing costs are computed today in

# Competitive summary invariants and edge cases

## Goal

Harden the competitive Turn Summary end-to-end: only the seats the closing
actually surfaced get rows, every non-competitive and non-interactive path keeps
today's pacing byte-for-byte, and the gate provably adds no save, no state
mutation and no RNG consumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eliminated seats produce no row (no ghost rows): the panel renders exactly the seats the closing surfaced, and a test asserts row-count and row-identity against an engine run with one eliminated seat.
2. N = 1 and single-player closings never present the competitive panel; the existing single-player `shouldGateTurnSummary` behaviour (deferred only, skipping reduced motion / tutorial / replay / competitive) is unchanged and covered by its existing tests.
3. Headless, AI-driven and Monte-Carlo paths never invoke the panel and keep the `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS` bounded pacing; a test drives a headless competitive day to the next day without an overlay surface and asserts it advances.
4. The gate adds no checkpoint save and mutates no engine state or RNG: `presentCompetitiveDayTail`'s save-before-closing ordering is asserted (save called exactly once, before the closing presentation), and the engine state is deep-equal (ignoring presentation fields) before and after the gate resolves.
5. Never stalls: when the model build throws, the competitive ledger is absent, or the scene has no `showTurnSummaryDialog` / overlay manager, the next day starts immediately, matching the pre-gate pacing.
6. Parent criterion delivered — Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the engine/headless close path; checkpoint save ordering (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged, and the dialog adds no save and mutates no state.

## Test-first checklist

- **Gate** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — eliminated seat omission; N=1/single-player skip; headless advance; save ordering; missing-surface fallback; state immutability and no extra RNG draws.

# Intake brief: Host memory pressure kills long-lived dev servers mid-session (swap exhaustion)

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** medium · **Cross-repo:** no (host action + tooling + docs) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVREB31W004F48D

**Producer decisions (2026-10-29):** Q1 = b (docs/runbook + committed read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`); Q2 = a (prune only confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered worktree dirs after listing; no process kills); Q3 = a (documented concurrency guideline + pre-start checks, no enforcement).

## Problem statement

Long-lived `vite --host` dev servers on this development host are dying mid-session, leaving the browser with `[vite] server connection lost`, failed HMR WebSocket retries and `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` for every card SVG / `csv-checksum.json` request. The host is under sustained memory pressure (swap essentially full) with many orphaned worktree checkouts and concurrent sibling workloads, but the exact kill mechanism is not yet confirmed. This item owns the **host-level remediation** that the diagnosis in `docs/dev/testing.md` explicitly defers to it.

## Users

- **Developers and agents running long-lived dev sessions** — need a `npm run dev` session to survive a working session so they can exercise the UI and HMR loop.
  - *User story:* "As a developer, I want my `vite --host` dev server to stay up for the duration of a session, so a mid-session asset flood does not force me to restart and lose my place."
- **Producer / on-call operator** — needs a safe, repeatable way to reclaim host memory (stale worktrees, orphaned servers) without risking uncommitted work.
  - *User story:* "As the operator, I want a documented, approval-gated hygiene procedure so I can reduce host pressure without deleting someone's in-progress work."
- **Agents running implement/test workflows** — depend on a stable dev server and watch budget on the host.
  - *User story:* "As an agent, I want concurrent `vite --host` servers capped and stale checkouts pruned so my test and dev runs are not starved or killed."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root-cause determination documented.** A findings section records, for each candidate cause, whether it is confirmed, ruled out, or undetermined, citing the commands and evidence used:
   - (a) kernel / `systemd-oomd` OOM kill of the `vite`/`node` process;
   - (b) manual or agent kill (including `wl cleanup-worktree`, which `implement.py finish`/`abort` invokes, and terminal/session termination);
   - (c) `:3000` port conflict (structurally a startup failure, not a mid-session kill).
   *Verification:* the finding is present in the work-item/docs and each hypothesis is explicitly resolved or marked undetermined with rationale.

2. **Safe worktree-hygiene procedure, committed helper, and evidenced execution (Q1 = b, Q2 = a).** A committed, read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` reports registered worktrees vs orphaned directories under `.worklog/worktrees`, swap/memory pressure, and orphaned dev servers; it never prunes or kills. A documented procedure distinguishes registered git worktrees (`git worktree list`) from orphaned directories, lists candidates for approval, and prunes **only** confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered directories — never `--force`, never registered worktrees, never stashes. Per Q2 (option a) the procedure is executed on this host and before/after counts are recorded (intake snapshot: **31 directories vs 15 registered worktrees including main → ~16 orphaned/unregistered**).
   *Verification:* the script runs on this host and reports the expected inventory; a test covers its detection logic; the procedure is present in docs and before/after counts are recorded as evidence.

3. **Dev-server concurrency cap and restart/swap-reclamation procedure documented (Q3 = a).** The existing `docs/dev/testing.md` troubleshooting section is extended with: pre-start checks (`free -m`, `swapon --show`, `ss -ltn | grep :3000`, process count), a documented cap on simultaneous `vite --host` servers across checkouts, and a step-by-step restart plus swap-reclamation procedure.
   *Verification:* the docs section exists and is cross-referenced from the README dev-server section.

4. **Post-remediation validation.** After the approved cleanup, record `free -m` / `swapon --show` before and after and confirm swap headroom improves, and confirm a dev session survives a documented soak (e.g. ≥30 min `npm run dev` with the card asset tree loaded) with no connection-lost cascade.
   *Verification:* before/after metrics plus the soak observation are recorded.

5. **Documentation and suite.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries. The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Environmental scope:** host actions, read-only tooling (`scripts/hygiene_check.sh`) and documentation; no product runtime behaviour change. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by the ship pipeline).
- **Destructive actions require explicit producer/operator approval:** removing worktree directories, killing processes, or deleting stashes. Never `git worktree prune --force`; never remove a registered worktree or a stash without triage.
- **Worktree isolation:** any committed change is made via the implement skill's worktree; `wl` and host commands run from the main checkout.
- **No ad-hoc test runs:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill.
- **Ignore rules:** `.worklog/*` is gitignored, so host evidence belongs in work-item comments, not committed files.

## Existing state

- **Memory:** swap **8187 / 8191 MB used (100 %)**; RAM 30 GB with ~12 GB available at intake time (`free -m`, `swapon --show`).
- **Worktrees:** 31 directories under `.worklog/worktrees`; `git worktree list` reports 15 worktrees including main (14 under `.worklog`) → ~16 orphaned/unregistered directories. Some are empty stubs (dated 7–10 Oct); others are full stale checkouts.
- **Concurrent sibling workloads observed:** `AI_Hell` vitest unit/integration plus a `vite preview --port 4173` (4 h+), `tce-the-rising` vitest browser (11 min), and many `ContextHub` `tsx` node processes (7 h+).
- **OOM evidence:** `systemd-oomd` active since 2026-10-18; **no kernel/oomd OOM-kill records on the current boot (18 Oct → now)**. The 729 OOM log lines all belong to the previous boot (2026-10-03: vitest workers, esbuild, dbus, systemd). So swap exhaustion at report time did **not** produce a kernel OOM kill on this boot.
- **Port:** no listener on `:3000` now — consistent with a dead server, not a bound/conflicting port. A mid-session port conflict is structurally implausible (Vite binds at startup).
- **Process tracking:** `wl cleanup-worktree` SIGTERMs tracked worktree-scoped processes; main-checkout dev servers are not tracked, and **0 processes were tracked** at intake.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/testing.md` already diagnoses the cascade ("Troubleshooting: dev server died mid-session") and explicitly defers host remediation to this item.
- **Gap (in scope, Q1 = b):** the global AGENTS.md workflow-hygiene rule references `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, which **does not exist** in this repo; this item adds it as a read-only detector.
- **Existing tooling:** the read-only `machine-hygiene` skill proposes kill/renice/prune actions but has no worktree pruning; the `cleanup` skill prunes branches, not worktrees.

## Desired change

1. A documented, evidence-backed root-cause determination (confirm or bound the kill cause).
2. Reduced host pressure: approval-gated pruning of orphaned worktrees, a committed read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, a documented concurrent-dev-server cap, and a restart/swap-reclamation runbook.
3. Recorded before/after host state so the improvement is verifiable.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/testing.md` — primary: extend the existing "dev server died mid-session" section into a host-pressure / worktree-hygiene runbook.
- `README.md` — cross-reference the restart procedure from the dev-server section (~line 220).
- `AGENTS.md` (repo) — optional cross-reference to the hygiene procedure.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — new read-only detector (worktree inventory, swap/memory pressure, orphaned dev servers); referenced by AGENTS.md but currently absent. Must include a focused test.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVREB31W004F48D** — Dev-session browser console errors: `/api/transcripts` 404 and dev-server drop cascade (completed). Source item; established the diagnosis and deferred host remediation here.
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** — Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (completed). Sibling host-pressure item; precedent for a diagnosis-plus-remediation chore.
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** / **MS-0MVSXXSMV003XKGI** — Vite watcher-ignore ports across sibling game repos. Adjacent watcher/worktree pressure work; explicitly out of scope here.
- **Skills:** `machine-hygiene` (read-only pressure analysis + approved remediation), `cleanup` (branch pruning), `test` (gated suite runs).
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/testing.md` (§ dev-server troubleshooting, § ENOSPC), `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Risks, assumptions, and failure modes

- **Data-loss risk:** pruning a worktree that holds uncommitted work. *Mitigation:* approval-gated, clean-only, registered-vs-orphaned check, `git status` per candidate, never `--force`.
- **Disruption risk:** killing a legitimately active dev server or test run. *Mitigation:* ancestry/age check and owner confirmation before any kill.
- **Scope-creep risk:** expanding into the watcher-ignore port family (MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0). *Mitigation:* record any extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Undetermined-cause risk:** the exact kill may be unrecoverable from available logs. *Mitigation:* AC1 requires "confirmed **or bounded**", not "prove OOM".
- **Assumption:** the affected dev server ran from the main checkout, so `wl cleanup-worktree` did not kill it. *Verify during implementation.*
- **Assumption:** log retention on the current boot covers the report window (verified: 18–29 Oct present).
- **Decision (Q3 = a):** "cap concurrent dev servers" is a documented guideline plus pre-start checks, not a new enforcement mechanism; no launcher/registry is added.
- **Tooling risk:** a new shell script without tests. *Mitigation:* keep it read-only and add a focused test for the inventory/classification logic.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed context plus repo/host research was sufficient to draft the initial brief, so no interactive round was held before drafting. The three decisions below were routed to the producer and answered on 2026-10-29.

- **Q1 — Delivery form for the guardrails?** Options: (a) docs/runbook only; (b) docs/runbook + a small committed `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` that reports stale worktrees, swap pressure, orphaned dev servers; (c) docs + a dev-server launcher wrapper.
  **Answer (producer):** **(b)** — docs/runbook plus a committed read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-29.
  **Recommended at draft time: (b)** — the global AGENTS.md already references `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, and a repeatable check is the durable fix.
  *Research:* file absent from repo; `machine-hygiene` covers process-level pressure but not worktree inventory.

- **Q2 — Approval to perform destructive host cleanup now?** Options: (a) prune only confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered directories after listing them; (b) also kill orphaned/abandoned dev servers; (c) detection only, defer all cleanup.
  **Answer (producer):** **(a)** — prune only confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered directories after listing them; no process kills. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-29.
  **Recommended at draft time: (a)**, then re-assess for (b) with an explicit list.

- **Q3 — Does "cap concurrent dev servers" need technical enforcement or a documented guideline?** Options: (a) documented guideline + pre-start checks; (b) a launcher/registry that refuses a second server; (c) no cap, restart procedure only.
  **Answer (producer):** **(a)** — documented guideline plus pre-start checks; no enforcement mechanism. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-29.
  **Recommended at draft time: (a)** — keeps the item environmental and non-speculative.

### Research performed

- Reviewed the current boot's kernel/oomd logs (`journalctl -b -g 'Out of memory|oom-kill|Killed process'`, `journalctl -u systemd-oomd`): no OOM kills since 2026-10-18; the 729 historical OOM lines are from the 2026-10-03 boot.
- Inventoried worktrees (`git worktree list` vs `.worklog/worktrees` directory count): 15 registered vs 31 directories.
- Inventoried live processes: sibling vitest/vite preview/serve and ContextHub node processes consuming memory.
- Read `docs/dev/testing.md` §§ dev-server troubleshooting / ENOSPC; confirmed this item is the deferred host-remediation follow-up.
- Inspected `wl cleanup-worktree` and `implement.py` `cleanup_worktree_processes` to characterise the agent-kill hypothesis.
- Ran the find-related skill (automated report merged above).

## Summary

Add `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts` to assert that no `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games` keys are declared in `package.json`, and that every `scaffold*` script's target file exists on disk.

None (runs against the live repo state).

- `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`
