## Problem

While finishing MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O the dev push ran **no** git hook:

- `git config --get core.hooksPath` → unset
- `.git/hooks/pre-push` → absent (only `post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite` plus `.sample` files)
- the repo's `.githooks/pre-push` exists but is never invoked from this checkout.

Consequences (the documented dev-push integration gates are inert here):

1. **No full-suite gate on dev pushes** — the framework documents the pre-push hook as the deterministic full-suite integration gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81); here a red tree can be pushed straight to `dev`. Note this repo's `.githooks/pre-push` in fact only enforces branch policy + context budget + worklog sync — it has no test-suite step at all — so even when wired it would not provide the documented gate.
2. **No protected-branch check** — a regular agent could push to `main`/`master` without the hook's refusal.
3. **No worklog auto-sync on push**.

## Why it matters

Agent push discipline (push only to `dev`, green suite before push, worklog sync) is currently enforced only by agent behaviour, not by the repository. Any audit that assumes "the hook ran the full suite" is relying on something that did not happen.

## Investigation starting points

- How hooks are installed (framework install script and `.githooks/` → `.git/hooks/` wiring) and why `pre-push` is missing here while `post-*` hooks are present.
- Whether `core.hooksPath` should be `.githooks` per clone (and re-set after a fresh clone/worktree).
- Whether `.githooks/pre-push` should gain the `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` step the framework docs describe.

## Out of scope

Fixing anything about MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O — that item is complete and its evidence came from an explicit `/skill:test` full-scope run.

# Re-scaffold the Main Street launcher to `Phaser.AUTO` and verify a clean WebGL boot once the core mask migration lands

Follow-up to `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (commit `73cfba6c`), raised on producer
instruction (2026-10-29, Q3: "ensure the TCE item created for 1 creates a work
item here when work is complete so that we can test and switch over").

## Problem statement

`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` migrated every **in-repo** `GeometryMask` clip to a
renderer-aware `ContainerClip` (Canvas `GeometryMask`, WebGL Mask filter) and
switched the launcher (`main.ts`) to `Phaser.AUTO`. Two gaps remain, both owned
by the core repo:

1. **Core-owned mask sites are still Canvas-only.** `core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`,
   `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts`, `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` and
   `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts` still call `setMask`
   with a `GeometryMask`, which is a **no-op under WebGL**. Those overlays
   therefore render unclipped in a WebGL boot.
   `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` currently
   **excludes** core-originated `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warnings —
   that exclusion is the standing marker of this gap.
2. **The scaffold generator still forces Canvas.** `main.ts` in this repo is
   auto-generated by `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderMainTs()`,
   which still emits `type: Phaser.CANVAS`. Running `npm run scaffold` would
   silently revert the `Phaser.AUTO` switch.

Both are tracked in the core work item **`CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I`**, which this
item is blocked by.

## Users

- **Game players** — Help / Settings / Overlay / Gym card-index scrolling must
  be visually correct (clipped) in the WebGL launcher, not just in Canvas.
- **Developers** — a re-scaffold must not silently revert the renderer, so the
  WebGL/GPU-shader path stays available.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Engine pin bumped.** `configs/engine-pin.json` pins the core commit that
   contains `CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I`, and `npm run engine:check` passes.
2. **Re-scaffold is stable.** `npm run scaffold` (or the repo's documented
   equivalent) is run and `main.ts` still boots with `type: Phaser.AUTO` — i.e.
   the regenerated file matches what the generator now emits, with no
   hand-edited drift. Confirm the file is not modified by a second scaffold run
   (idempotent).
3. **WebGL test hardened.** In
   `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` the
   `inRepoCanvasOnlyWarnings()` core-path exclusion is removed, so the test
   asserts **zero** `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warnings from any source
   in a real WebGL boot of `MainStreetScene` and `GymCardIndexScene`.
4. **WebGL boot verified.** The launcher boots on the WebGL renderer with the
   Help panel, Settings panel, overlay dialogs and the Gym card index all
   clipping correctly (pixel-probe or scene-graph evidence in the browser test,
   plus a manual smoke note in the work-item comments).
5. **Suite green.** Full project test suite passes, including the Canvas-pinned
   browser tests (which must stay on `Phaser.CANVAS` for CI speed).
6. **Docs updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` no longer describes the core-path
   warning exclusion; `src/README.md` "Viewport clipping" no longer lists the
   core sites as deferred, and notes that the whole pipeline is now
   renderer-aware.

## Constraints

- Do **not** edit the `core` submodule from this repo — bump the pin and
  consume the released core change.
- Canvas rendering output must remain unchanged.
- Browser tests stay on `Phaser.CANVAS` except the dedicated WebGL test.

## Related work

- `CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I` (core) — the prerequisite: core mask migration + the
  scaffold generator emitting `Phaser.AUTO`.
- `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` — delivered the in-repo renderer-aware clipping, the
  WebGL browser test and the `Phaser.AUTO` launcher switch.
- `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW` — the earlier core-deferral record, superseded by
  `CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I`.
data.title: Re-scaffold Main Street launcher to Phaser.AUTO and verify a clean WebGL boot once core masks land
